Herein, this is the essence: the fixed order of consciousness—such as the mind-element arising immediately after eye-consciousness, and the mind-consciousness-element arising immediately after the mind-element, etc.—succeeds only through the power of the immediately preceding consciousness, and not otherwise. Therefore, a phenomenon capable of producing the arising of a suitable consciousness immediately after itself is the proximity-condition. For that reason, He said: “By proximity-condition: the eye-consciousness element and its associated states are a condition for the mind-element and its associated states by way of proximity-condition,” and so on (Paṭṭhāna 1.1.4). Whatever is the proximity-condition is itself the contiguity-condition. The difference here is merely in the letter, as with accumulation and continuity, and as with the dyads of designation and expression, etc. In meaning, however, there is no difference.

Yampi “atthānantaratāya anantarapaccayo, kālānantaratāya samanantarapaccayo”ti ācariyānaṃ mataṃ, taṃ “nirodhā vuṭṭhahantassa nevasaññānāsaññāyatanakusalaṃ phalasamāpattiyā samanantarapaccayena paccayo”tiādīhi (paṭṭhā. 1.1.418) virujjhati. Yampi tattha vadanti “dhammānaṃ samuṭṭhāpanasamatthatā na parihāyati, bhāvanābalena pana vāritattā dhammā samanantarā nuppajjantī”ti, tampi kālānantaratāya abhāvameva sādheti. Bhāvanābalena hi tattha kālānantaratā natthīti, mayampi etadeva vadāma. Yasmā ca kālānantaratā natthi, tasmā samanantarapaccayatā na yujjati. Kālānantaratāya hi tesaṃ samanantarapaccayo hotīti laddhi. Tasmā [V 2.0164] abhinivesaṃ akatvā byañjanamattatovettha nānākaraṇaṃ paccetabbaṃ, na atthato. Kathaṃ? Natthi etesaṃ antaranti hi anantarā. Saṇṭhānābhāvato suṭṭhu anantarāti samanantarā.

The teachers’ view that “it is the proximity-condition due to immediacy in substance, and the contiguity-condition due to immediacy in time” is contradicted by statements such as “for one emerging from cessation, the wholesome state of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is a condition for the attainment of fruition by way of contiguity-condition” (Paṭṭhāna 1.1.418). Furthermore, what they say in that regard—“the capacity to produce states does not decline, but because they are prevented by the power of development, states do not arise contiguously”—also establishes the absence of immediacy in time. For there, due to the power of development, there is no immediacy in time; this is precisely what we say. And because there is no immediacy in time, contiguity-conditionality is not tenable. For their doctrine is that it is a contiguity-condition because of immediacy in time. Therefore, without adhering to this view, one should accept the difference here as merely verbal, not in meaning. How so? “There is no interval for them”—thus they are proximate (anantarā). “Because of the absence of any formation between them, they are thoroughly proximate”—thus they are contiguous (samanantarā).

599. Uppajjamānova saha uppādanabhāvena upakārako dhammo sahajātapaccayo pakāsassa padīpo viya. So arūpakkhandhādivasena chabbidho hoti. Yathāha – “cattāro khandhā arūpino aññamaññaṃ sahajātapaccayena paccayo. Cattāro mahābhūtā aññamaññaṃ, okkantikkhaṇe nāmarūpaṃ aññamaññaṃ, cittacetasikā dhammā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ, mahābhūtā upādārūpānaṃ, rūpino dhammā arūpīnaṃ dhammānaṃ kiñcikāle sahajātapaccayena paccayo, kiñcikāle na sahajātapaccayena paccayo”ti (paṭṭhā. 1.1.6). Idaṃ hadayavatthumeva sandhāya vuttaṃ.

599. A phenomenon that, while itself arising, is helpful by way of causing other phenomena to arise together with it, is the co-nascence condition, like a lamp for light. It is of six kinds by way of the immaterial aggregates and so forth. As it is said: “The four immaterial aggregates are a condition for each other by co-nascence. The four great elements are a condition for each other. At the moment of conception, mentality and materiality are a condition for each other. Consciousness and mental factors are a condition for consciousness-originated materiality. The great elements are a condition for derived materiality. Material phenomena are at certain times a condition for immaterial phenomena by co-nascence, and at certain times are not a condition by co-nascence” (Paṭṭhāna 1.1.6). This was said with reference only to the heart-base.

600. Aññamaññaṃ [M 2.0167] uppādanupatthambhanabhāvena upakārako dhammo aññamaññapaccayo aññamaññūpatthambhakaṃ tidaṇḍakaṃ viya. So arūpakkhandhādivasena tividho hoti. Yathāha – “cattāro khandhā arūpino aññamaññapaccayena paccayo. Cattāro mahābhūtā okkantikkhaṇe nāmarūpaṃ aññamaññapaccayena paccayo”ti (paṭṭhā. 1.1.7).

600. A phenomenon that is helpful by way of mutual production and support is the mutuality condition, like the three sticks of a tripod supporting one another. It is of three kinds by way of the immaterial aggregates and so forth. As it is said: “The four immaterial aggregates are a condition for each other by mutuality condition. The four great elements are a condition for each other. At the moment of conception, mentality and materiality are a condition for each other by mutuality condition” (Paṭṭhāna 1.1.7).

601. Adhiṭṭhānākārena nissayākārena ca upakārako dhammo nissayapaccayo tarucittakammādīnaṃ pathavīpaṭādayo viya. So “cattāro khandhā arūpino aññamaññaṃ nissayapaccayena paccayo”ti evaṃ sahajāte vuttanayeneva veditabbo. Chaṭṭho panettha koṭṭhāso “cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyā…pe… sota… ghāna… jivhā… kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ nissayapaccayena paccayo. Yaṃ rūpaṃ nissāya manodhātu ca manoviññāṇadhātu ca vattanti, taṃ rūpaṃ manodhātuyā ca manoviññāṇadhātuyā ca taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ nissayapaccayena paccayo”ti (paṭṭhā. 1.1.8) evaṃ vibhatto.

601. A phenomenon that is helpful by way of being a foundation and by way of being a support is the support condition, like the earth and cloth for trees, paintings, and so forth. It should be understood in the same way as was stated for the co-nascence condition, thus: “The four immaterial aggregates are a condition for each other by support condition,” and so on. Here, however, the sixth part is distinguished thus: “The eye-base is a condition for the eye-consciousness element and its associated phenomena by support condition… and so on… The ear-base… nose-base… tongue-base… body-base is a condition for the body-consciousness element and its associated phenomena by support condition. That materiality which, being depended upon, the mind-element and the mind-consciousness element occur—that materiality is a condition for the mind-element, for the mind-consciousness element, and for their associated phenomena by support condition” (Paṭṭhāna 1.1.8).

602. Upanissayapaccayoti ettha pana ayaṃ tāva vacanattho, tadadhīnavuttitāya attano phalena nissito na paṭikkhittoti nissayo. Yathā pana bhuso āyāso upāyāso, evaṃ bhuso nissayo upanissayo, balavakāraṇassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Tasmā balavakāraṇabhāvena upakārako dhammo upanissayapaccayoti veditabbo.

602. Now, as to the term ‘decisive support condition,’ first, this is the word-meaning: a ‘support’ (nissaya) is so called because it is depended upon and not rejected by its own result, since the result’s existence is dependent on it. And just as intense exertion (āyāso) is upāyāso, so too a strong support (nissayo) is upanissayo. This is a synonym for a powerful cause. Therefore, a phenomenon that is helpful by way of being a powerful cause should be understood as the decisive support condition.

So [V 2.0165] ārammaṇūpanissayo anantarūpanissayo pakatūpanissayoti tividho hoti. Tattha “dānaṃ datvā sīlaṃ samādiyitvā uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ garuṃkatvā paccavekkhati, pubbe suciṇṇāni garuṃkatvā paccavekkhati, jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā jhānaṃ garuṃkatvā paccavekkhati, sekkhā gotrabhuṃ garuṃkatvā paccavekkhanti, vodānaṃ garuṃkatvā paccavekkhanti. Sekkhā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ garuṃkatvā paccavekkhantī”ti (paṭṭhā. 1.1.423) evamādinā nayena ārammaṇūpanissayo tāva ārammaṇādhipatinā saddhiṃ nānattaṃ akatvāva vibhatto. Tattha yaṃ ārammaṇaṃ garuṃkatvā cittacetasikā uppajjanti, taṃ niyamato tesu ārammaṇesu balavārammaṇaṃ hoti. Iti garukattabbamattaṭṭhena [M 2.0168] ārammaṇādhipati, balavakāraṇaṭṭhena ārammaṇūpanissayoti evametesaṃ nānattaṃ veditabbaṃ.

It is of three kinds: object decisive support, contiguity decisive support, and natural decisive support. Among these, the object decisive support is first explained without making a distinction from the object predominance condition, in the manner beginning thus: “Having given a gift, undertaken the precepts, or performed the Uposatha observance, one reflects on it, holding it in high esteem; one reflects on previously well-practiced deeds, holding them in high esteem; having emerged from jhāna, one reflects on the jhāna, holding it in high esteem; trainees reflect on the change-of-lineage consciousness (gotrabhū), holding it in high esteem; they reflect on the purification (vodāna), holding it in high esteem. Trainees, having emerged from the path, reflect on the path, holding it in high esteem” (Paṭṭhāna 1.1.423). Therein, whatever object is held in high esteem when consciousness and mental factors arise, that object is, by rule, a powerful one among their objects. Thus, the distinction between these two should be understood as follows: in the sense of being merely an object to be held in high esteem, it is object predominance; in the sense of being a powerful cause, it is object decisive support.

Anantarūpanissayopi “purimā purimā kusalā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ kusalānaṃ khandhānaṃ upanissayapaccayena paccayo”tiādinā (paṭṭhā. 1.1.9) nayena anantarapaccayena saddhiṃ nānattaṃ akatvāva vibhatto. Mātikānikkhepe pana nesaṃ “cakkhuviññāṇadhātu taṃsampayuttakā ca dhammā manodhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo”tiādinā (paṭṭhā. 1.1.4) nayena anantarassa, “purimā purimā kusalā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ upanissayapaccayena paccayo”tiādinā (paṭṭhā. 1.1.9) nayena upanissayassa āgatattā nikkhepe viseso atthi. Sopi atthato ekībhāvameva gacchati. Evaṃ santepi attano attano anantarā anurūpassa cittuppādassa pavattanasamatthatāya anantaratā, purimacittassa pacchimacittuppādane balavatāya anantarūpanissayatā veditabbā. Yathā hi hetupaccayādīsu kiñci dhammaṃ vināpi cittaṃ uppajjati, na evaṃ anantaracittaṃ vinā cittassa uppatti nāma atthi. Tasmā balavapaccayo hoti. Iti attano attano anantarā anurūpacittuppādanavasena anantarapaccayo, balavakāraṇavasena anantarūpanissayoti evametesaṃ nānattaṃ veditabbaṃ.

The contiguity decisive support is also explained without making a distinction from the contiguity condition, in the manner beginning with: “The preceding wholesome aggregates are a condition for the succeeding wholesome aggregates by way of the decisive support condition” (Paṭṭhāna 1.1.9). However, in the exposition of the matrix, there is a distinction between them. For the contiguity condition, it is stated in the manner beginning with: “The eye-consciousness element and its associated phenomena are a condition for the mind-element and its associated phenomena by way of the contiguity condition” (Paṭṭhāna 1.1.4). For the decisive support condition, it is stated in the manner beginning with: “The preceding wholesome phenomena are a condition for the succeeding wholesome phenomena by way of the decisive support condition” (Paṭṭhāna 1.1.9). Even so, in meaning, they become one and the same. Despite this, the state of contiguity should be understood as the capacity of each immediately preceding consciousness to cause the occurrence of a corresponding consciousness, while the state of contiguity decisive support should be understood as the power of the preceding consciousness in producing the subsequent consciousness. For just as consciousness arises even without some phenomena, such as the root condition, so there is no such thing as the arising of consciousness without an immediately preceding consciousness. Therefore, it is a powerful condition. Thus, the distinction between them should be understood as follows: by way of producing a corresponding consciousness immediately after itself, it is the contiguity condition; by way of being a powerful cause, it is the contiguity decisive support condition.

Pakatūpanissayo pana pakato upanissayo pakatūpanissayo. Pakato nāma attano santāne nipphādito vā saddhāsīlādi upasevito vā utubhojanādi. Pakatiyā eva vā upanissayo pakatūpanissayo, ārammaṇānantarehi asammissoti attho. Tassa pakatūpanissayo “saddhaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti, sīlaṃ samādiyati, uposathakammaṃ karoti, jhānaṃ uppādeti, vipassanaṃ [V 2.0166] uppādeti, maggaṃ uppādeti, abhiññaṃ uppādeti, samāpattiṃ uppādeti. Sīlaṃ, sutaṃ, cāgaṃ, paññaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti. Saddhā, sīlaṃ, sutaṃ, cāgo, paññā saddhāya, sīlassa, sutassa, cāgassa, paññāya, upanissayapaccayena paccayo”tiādinā (paṭṭhā. 1.1.423) nayena anekappakārato pabhedo veditabbo. Iti ime saddhādayo pakatā ceva balavakāraṇaṭṭhena upanissayā cāti pakatūpanissayoti.

Now, as for established decisive support: a well-prepared, strong cause is an established decisive support. 'Well-prepared' refers to that which is produced in one's own continuum, such as faith, virtue, and so on, or that which is cultivated, such as suitable climate, food, and so on. Alternatively, a strong cause by its very nature is an established decisive support; the meaning is that it is unmixed with object and proximity conditions. The classification of this established decisive support should be understood in many ways according to the method beginning with: 'Relying on faith, one gives a gift, undertakes moral virtue, performs the observance day duties, develops absorption, develops insight, develops the path, develops direct knowledge, develops attainment. Relying on moral virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom, one gives a gift… and so on… develops attainment. Faith, moral virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom are a condition for faith, for moral virtue, for learning, for generosity, and for wisdom by way of decisive support condition.' Thus, these qualities beginning with faith are both well-prepared and are decisive supports in the sense of being a strong cause; therefore, they are called 'established decisive support'.

603. Paṭhamataraṃ [M 2.0169] uppajjitvā vattamānabhāvena upakārako dhammo purejātapaccayo. So pañcadvāre vatthārammaṇahadayavatthuvasena ekādasavidho hoti. Yathāha – “cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. Sota…pe… ghāna, jivhā, kāyāyatanaṃ, rūpa, sadda, gandha, rasa, phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. Rūpa, sadda, gandha, rasa, phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ manodhātuyā. Yaṃ rūpaṃ nissāya manodhātu ca manoviññāṇadhātu ca vattanti, taṃ rūpaṃ manodhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. Manoviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ kiñcikāle purejātapaccayena paccayo. Kiñcikāle na purejātapaccayena paccayo”ti (paṭṭhā. 1.1.10).

603. A state that assists by having arisen first and being present is the pre-nascence condition. In the five sense-doors, it is of eleven kinds by way of physical bases, objects, and the heart-base. As it is said: “The eye-base is a condition for the eye-consciousness element and its associated states by way of the pre-nascence condition. The ear… and so on… nose, tongue, body-base; visible form, sound, odor, taste, and tangible object are a condition for the body-consciousness element and its associated states by way of the pre-nascence condition. Visible form, sound, odor, taste, and tangible object are a condition for the mind-element. That material form depending on which the mind-element and the mind-consciousness element occur, that material form is a condition for the mind-element and its associated states by way of the pre-nascence condition. For the mind-consciousness element and its associated states, it is a condition by way of pre-nascence condition at a certain time; it is not a condition by way of pre-nascence condition at a certain time.”

604. Purejātānaṃ rūpadhammānaṃ upatthambhakattena upakārako arūpadhammo pacchājātapaccayo gijjhapotakasarīrānaṃ āhārāsācetanā viya. Tena vuttaṃ “pacchājātā cittacetasikā dhammā purejātassa imassa kāyassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo”ti (paṭṭhā. 1.1.11).

604. An immaterial state that assists by way of supporting previously arisen material states is the post-nascence condition, like the volition of desire for food for the bodies of young vultures. Therefore, it is said: “Subsequently arisen consciousness and mental factors are a condition for this previously arisen body by way of the post-nascence condition.”

605. Āsevanaṭṭhena anantarānaṃ paguṇabalavabhāvāya upakārako dhammo āsevanapaccayo ganthādīsu purimapurimābhiyogo viya. So kusalākusalakiriyajavanavasena tividho hoti. Yathāha – “purimā purimā kusalā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ āsevanapaccayena paccayo. Purimā purimā akusalā…pe… kiriyābyākatā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ kiriyābyākatānaṃ dhammānaṃ āsevanapaccayena paccayo”ti (paṭṭhā. 1.1.12).

605. A state that assists by way of repetition for the purpose of making the immediately succeeding states proficient and strong is the repetition condition, like the preceding and repeated application to texts and so on. It is threefold by way of wholesome, unwholesome, and functional javana. As it is said: “Preceding wholesome states are a condition for succeeding wholesome states by way of the repetition condition. Preceding unwholesome states… and so on… preceding functional indeterminate states are a condition for succeeding functional indeterminate states by way of the repetition condition.”

606. Cittapayogasaṅkhātena kiriyabhāvena upakārako dhammo kammapaccayo. So nānakkhaṇikāya ceva kusalākusalacetanāya sahajātāya ca sabbāyapi cetanāya vasena duvidho hoti[V 2.0167]. Yathāha – “kusalākusalaṃ kammaṃ vipākānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. Cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ dhammānaṃ taṃsamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo”ti (paṭṭhā. 1.1.13).

606. A state that assists by way of being an action, which is reckoned as mental application, is the kamma condition. It is twofold: by way of wholesome and unwholesome volition that is of different moments, and by way of all co-nascent volition. As it is said: “Wholesome and unwholesome kamma is a condition for the resultant aggregates and for kamma-produced materiality by way of the kamma condition. Volition is a condition for its associated states and for the materiality produced by them by way of the kamma condition.”

607. Nirussāhasantabhāvena [M 2.0170] nirussāhasantabhāvāya upakārako vipākadhammo vipākapaccayo. So pavatte taṃsamuṭṭhānānaṃ, paṭisandhiyaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ, sabbattha ca sampayuttadhammānaṃ paccayo hoti. Yathāha –“vipākābyākato eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ vipākapaccayena paccayo…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe vipākābyākato eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ. Tayo khandhā ekassa khandhassa. Dve khandhā dvinnaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ vipākapaccayena paccayo. Khandhā vatthussa vipākapaccayena paccayo”ti.

607. A resultant state that assists by its tranquil and effortless nature for the sake of a tranquil and effortless nature is the resultant condition. It is a condition for the materiality produced by it during the course of life, for kamma-produced materiality at rebirth-linking, and in all cases for its associated mental states. As it is said: “One resultant-indeterminate aggregate is a condition for three aggregates and for mind-produced materiality by way of the resultant condition… and so on… At the moment of rebirth-linking, one resultant-indeterminate aggregate is a condition for three aggregates and for kamma-produced materiality. Three aggregates are a condition for one aggregate. Two aggregates are a condition for two aggregates and for kamma-produced materiality by way of the resultant condition. The aggregates are a condition for the physical base by way of the resultant condition.”

608. Rūpārūpānaṃ upatthambhakaṭṭhena upakārakā cattāro āhārā āhārapaccayo. Yathāha –“kabaḷīkāro āhāro imassa kāyassa āhārapaccayena paccayo. Arūpino āhārā sampayuttakānaṃ dhammānaṃ taṃsamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ āhārapaccayena paccayo”ti (paṭṭhā. 1.1.15). Pañhāvāre pana “paṭisandhikkhaṇe vipākābyākatā āhārā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ āhārapaccayena paccayo”tipi (paṭṭhā. 1.1.429) vuttaṃ.

608. The four nutriments, which assist by way of supporting material and immaterial states, are the nutriment condition. As it is said: “Edible food is a condition for this body by way of the nutriment condition. Immaterial nutriments are a condition for their associated states and for the materiality produced by them by way of the nutriment condition.” In the Question Section, however, it is also said: “At the moment of rebirth-linking, resultant-indeterminate nutriments are a condition for their associated aggregates and for kamma-produced materiality by way of the nutriment condition.”

609. Adhipatiyaṭṭhena upakārakā itthindriyapurisindriyavajjā vīsatindriyā indriyapaccayo. Tattha cakkhundriyādayo arūpadhammānaṃyeva, sesā rūpārūpānaṃ paccayā honti. Yathāha – “cakkhundriyaṃ cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyā…pe… sota… ghāna… jivhā… kāyindriyaṃ kāyaviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayo. Rūpajīvitindriyaṃ kaṭattārūpānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayo. Arūpino indriyā sampayuttakānaṃ dhammānaṃ taṃsamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayo”ti (paṭṭhā. 1.1.16). Pañhāvāre pana “paṭisandhikkhaṇe vipākābyākatā indriyā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayo”tipi (paṭṭhā. 1.1.430) vuttaṃ.

609. The twenty faculties, excluding the femininity faculty and the masculinity faculty, being helpful by way of dominance, are the faculty condition. Among them, the eye faculty and so forth are conditions only for immaterial phenomena, while the remaining faculties are conditions for both material and immaterial phenomena. As it is said: “The eye faculty is a condition for the eye-consciousness element…pe… the ear… the nose… the tongue… the body faculty is a condition for the body-consciousness element and for the states associated with them by way of the faculty condition. The material life faculty is a condition for kamma-produced materiality by way of the faculty condition. The immaterial faculties are a condition for the associated states and for the materiality produced thereby by way of the faculty condition” (Paṭṭh. 1.1.16). In the section on questions, it is also said: “At the moment of rebirth-linking, resultant-indeterminate faculties are a condition for the associated aggregates and for kamma-produced materiality by way of the faculty condition” (Paṭṭh. 1.1.430).

610. Upanijjhāyanaṭṭhena upakārakāni ṭhapetvā dvipañcaviññāṇe sukhadukkhavedanādvayaṃ sabbānipi [V 2.0168] kusalādibhedāni satta jhānaṅgāni jhānapaccayo. Yathāha –“jhānaṅgāni jhānasampayuttakānaṃ dhammānaṃ taṃsamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ jhānapaccayena [M 2.0171] paccayo”ti (paṭṭhā. 1.1.17). Pañhāvāre pana “paṭisandhikkhaṇe vipākābyākatāni jhānaṅgāni sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ jhānapaccayena paccayo”tipi (paṭṭhā. 1.1.431) vuttaṃ.

610. The seven jhana factors, classified as wholesome and so forth, being helpful by way of close contemplation, are the jhana condition, excluding the two feelings of pleasure and pain in the two sets of fivefold consciousnesses. As it is said: “The jhana factors are a condition for the states associated with jhana and for the materiality produced thereby by way of the jhana condition” (Paṭṭh. 1.1.17). In the section on questions, it is also stated: “At the moment of rebirth-linking, resultant-indeterminate jhana factors are a condition for the associated aggregates and for kamma-produced materiality by way of the jhana condition” (Paṭṭh. 1.1.431).

611. Yato tato vā niyyānaṭṭhena upakārakāni kusalādibhedāni dvādasa maggaṅgāni maggapaccayo. Yathāha – “maggaṅgāni maggasampayuttakānaṃ dhammānaṃ taṃsamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ maggapaccayena paccayo”ti (paṭṭhā. 1.1.18). Pañhāvāre pana “paṭisandhikkhaṇe vipākābyākatāni maggaṅgāni sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ maggapaccayena paccayo”tipi (paṭṭhā. 1.1.432) vuttaṃ. Ete pana dvepi jhānamaggapaccayā dvipañcaviññāṇāhetukacittesu na labbhantīti veditabbā.

611. The twelve path factors, classified as wholesome and so forth, being helpful by way of leading out, whether rightly or wrongly, are the path condition. As it is said: “The path factors are a condition for the states associated with the path and for the materiality produced thereby by way of the path condition” (Paṭṭh. 1.1.18). In the section on questions, it is also said: “At the moment of rebirth-linking, resultant-indeterminate path factors are a condition for the associated aggregates and for kamma-produced materiality by way of the path condition” (Paṭṭh. 1.1.432). However, it should be understood that these two, the jhana and path conditions, are not found in the two sets of fivefold consciousnesses and in rootless consciousnesses.

612. Ekavatthukaekārammaṇaekuppādekanirodhasaṅkhātena sampayuttabhāvena upakārakā arūpadhammā sampayuttapaccayo. Yathāha – “cattāro khandhā arūpino aññamaññaṃ sampayuttapaccayena paccayo”ti (paṭṭhā. 1.1.19).

612. Immaterial phenomena, being helpful by way of their association, which is characterized by having one basis, one object, one arising, and one ceasing, are the associated condition. As it is said: “The four immaterial aggregates are a condition for one another by way of the associated condition” (Paṭṭh. 1.1.19).

613. Ekavatthukādibhāvānupagamena upakārakā rūpino dhammā arūpīnaṃ dhammānaṃ, arūpinopi rūpīnaṃ vippayuttapaccayo. So sahajātapacchājātapurejātavasena tividho hoti. Vuttañhetaṃ “sahajātā kusalā khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā kusalā khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo”ti (paṭṭhā. 1.1.434). Abyākatapadassa pana sahajātavibhaṅge “paṭisandhikkhaṇe vipākābyākatā khandhā kaṭattārūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Khandhā vatthussa. Vatthu khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo”tipi (paṭṭhā. 1.1.434) vuttaṃ. Purejātaṃ pana cakkhundriyādivatthuvaseneva veditabbaṃ. Yathāha – “purejātaṃ cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Vatthu vipākābyākatānaṃ kiriyābyākatānaṃ khandhānaṃ…pe… vatthu kusalānaṃ khandhānaṃ…pe… vatthu akusalānaṃ khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo”ti (paṭṭhā. 1.1.434).

613. Material phenomena, being helpful by not sharing a single basis and so forth, are the dissociated condition for immaterial phenomena, and immaterial phenomena are likewise for material phenomena. This is threefold: co-arisen, post-arisen, and pre-arisen. For it is said: “Co-arisen wholesome aggregates are a condition for mind-produced materiality by way of the dissociated condition. Post-arisen wholesome aggregates are a condition for this pre-arisen body by way of the dissociated condition” (Paṭṭh. 1.1.434). In the co-arisen analysis of the indeterminate term, it is also said: “At the moment of rebirth-linking, resultant-indeterminate aggregates are a condition for kamma-produced materiality by way of the dissociated condition. Aggregates are a condition for the base. The base is a condition for the aggregates by way of the dissociated condition” (Paṭṭh. 1.1.434). The pre-arisen, however, should be understood only in terms of the base consisting of the eye faculty and so forth. As it is said: “The pre-arisen eye base is a condition for eye-consciousness by way of the dissociated condition…pe… the body base is a condition for body-consciousness. The base is a condition for resultant-indeterminate and functional-indeterminate aggregates…pe… the base is a condition for wholesome aggregates…pe… the base is a condition for unwholesome aggregates by way of the dissociated condition” (Paṭṭh. 1.1.434).

614. Paccuppannalakkhaṇena [V 2.0169] atthibhāvena tādisasseva dhammassa upatthambhakattena upakārako dhammo atthipaccayo. Tassa arūpakkhandhamahābhūtanāmarūpacittacetasikamahābhūtaāyatanavatthuvasena sattadhā mātikā [M 2.0172] nikkhittā. Yathāha –“cattāro khandhā arūpino aññamaññaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo, cattāro mahābhūtā, okkantikkhaṇe nāmarūpaṃ aññamaññaṃ. Cittacetasikā dhammā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ. Mahābhūtā upādārūpānaṃ. Cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyā…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ…pe… rūpāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Rūpāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ manodhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ. Yaṃ rūpaṃ nissāya manodhātu ca manoviññāṇadhātu ca vattanti, taṃ rūpaṃ manodhātuyā ca manoviññāṇadhātuyā ca taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo”ti (paṭṭhā. 1.1.21).

614. A phenomenon that is helpful by supporting another such phenomenon through its state of presence, which has the characteristic of being present, is the presence condition. Its matrix is set forth in seven ways: by way of immaterial aggregates, great elements, name-and-form, mind and mental factors, great elements, sense bases, and the base. As it is said: “The four immaterial aggregates are a condition for one another by way of the presence condition. The four great elements are a condition for one another. At the moment of conception, name-and-form are a condition for one another. Mind and mental factors are a condition for mind-produced materiality. The great elements are a condition for derived materiality. The eye base is a condition for the eye-consciousness element…pe… the body base…pe… the visible form base…pe… the tangible base is a condition for the body-consciousness element and for the states associated with it by way of the presence condition. The visible form base…pe… the tangible base is a condition for the mind element and for the states associated with it. The material form on which the mind element and mind-consciousness element depend is a condition for the mind element, the mind-consciousness element, and the states associated with them by way of the presence condition” (Paṭṭh. 1.1.21).

Pañhāvāre pana sahajātaṃ purejātaṃ pacchājātaṃ āhāraṃ indriyantipi nikkhipitvā sahajāte tāva “eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ taṃsamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo”tiādinā (paṭṭhā. 1.1.435) nayena niddeso kato, purejāte purejātānaṃ cakkhādīnaṃ vasena niddeso kato. Pacchājāte purejātassa imassa kāyassa pacchājātānaṃ cittacetasikānaṃ paccayavasena niddeso kato. Āhārindriyesu “kabaḷīkāro āhāro imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Rūpajīvitindriyaṃ kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo”ti (paṭṭhā. 1.1.435) evaṃ niddeso katoti.

In the Question Section, however, having also set forth co-nascence, pre-nascence, post-nascence, nutriment, and faculty, firstly, regarding co-nascence, the exposition is made in the manner beginning with: “One aggregate is a condition for the three aggregates and for the materiality originated therefrom by presence condition,” and so on. Regarding pre-nascence, the exposition is made by way of the pre-nascent eye, and so forth. Regarding post-nascence, the exposition is made by way of the conditionality of post-nascent mind and mental factors for this pre-nascent body. Regarding nutriment and faculty, the exposition is made thus: “Edible food is a condition for this body by presence condition. The material life faculty is a condition for kamma-produced materiality by presence condition.” Thus the exposition is made.

615. Attano anantarā uppajjamānānaṃ arūpadhammānaṃ pavattiokāsadānena upakārakā samanantaraniruddhā arūpadhammā natthipaccayo. Yathāha –“samanantaraniruddhā cittacetasikā dhammā paṭuppannānaṃ cittacetasikānaṃ dhammānaṃ natthipaccayena paccayo”ti.

615. Immediately ceased immaterial phenomena, which are helpful by giving the opportunity for arising to the immaterial phenomena arising immediately after them, are the absence condition. As it is said: “Immediately ceased mind and mental factors are a condition for presently arisen mind and mental factors by way of the absence condition.”

Te eva vigatabhāvena upakārakattā vigatapaccayo. Yathāha – “samanantaravigatā cittacetasikā dhammā paṭuppannānaṃ cittacetasikānaṃ dhammānaṃ vigatapaccayena paccayo”ti.

Those very same states, being helpful by way of their having disappeared, are the disappearance condition. As it is said: “Immediately disappeared mind and mental factors are a condition for presently arisen mind and mental factors by way of the disappearance condition.”

Atthi paccayadhammā eva ca avigatabhāvena upakārakattā avigatapaccayoti veditabbā. Desanāvilāsena [V 2.0170] pana tathā vinetabbaveneyyavasena vā ayaṃ duko vutto, ahetukadukaṃ vatvāpi hetuvippayuttaduko viyāti.

And the very same states of the presence condition, being helpful by way of their not having disappeared, should be understood as the non-disappearance condition. However, this pair is stated for the sake of elegance in the teaching, or in accordance with the capacity of those to be trained, just as the pair of states dissociated from a root is stated even after the rootless pair has been stated.

Avijjāpaccayāsaṅkhārapadavitthārakathā

The Detailed Exposition of the Clause ‘With Ignorance as Condition, Formations’

616. Evamimesu [M 2.0173] catuvīsatiyā paccayesu ayaṃ avijjā,

616. Thus, among these twenty-four conditions, this ignorance:

Paccayo hoti puññānaṃ, duvidhānekadhā pana;

Paresaṃ pacchimānaṃ sā, ekadhā paccayo matāti.

Is a condition for meritorious formations in two ways; for the others, however, in many ways. For the final ones, that ignorance is considered a condition in one way.

Tattha puññānaṃ duvidhāti ārammaṇapaccayena ca upanissayapaccayena cāti dvedhā paccayo hoti. Sā hi avijjaṃ khayato vayato sammasanakāle kāmāvacarānaṃ puññābhisaṅkhārānaṃ ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo hoti. Abhiññācittena samohacittaṃ jānanakāle rūpāvacarānaṃ. Avijjāsamatikkamatthāya pana dānādīni ceva kāmāvacarapuññakiriyavatthūni pūrentassa, rūpāvacarajjhānāni ca uppādentassa dvinnampi tesaṃ upanissayapaccayena paccayo hoti. Tathā avijjāsammūḷhattā kāmabhavarūpabhavasampattiyo patthetvā tāneva puññāni karontassa.

Therein, ‘in two ways for meritorious formations’ means it is a condition in two ways: by object condition and by decisive support condition. For, when one contemplates ignorance as subject to destruction and decay, it is a condition by way of object condition for the meritorious formations of the sense sphere. When knowing a mind accompanied by delusion with a mind of direct knowledge, it is so for those of the form sphere. Furthermore, for one who fulfills the grounds for meritorious action of the sense sphere, such as giving, for the purpose of overcoming ignorance, and for one who develops the form-sphere absorptions, it is a condition for both of them by way of decisive support condition. Likewise for one who, being deluded by ignorance, aspires to the attainments of sense-sphere existence and form-sphere existence and performs those same meritorious deeds.

Anekadhā pana paresanti apuññābhisaṅkhārānaṃ anekadhā paccayo hoti. Kathaṃ? Esā hi avijjaṃ ārabbha rāgādīnaṃ uppajjanakāle ārammaṇapaccayena, garuṃkatvā assādanakāle ārammaṇādhipatiārammaṇūpanissayehi, avijjāsammūḷhassa anādīnavadassāvino pāṇātipātādīni karontassa upanissayapaccayena, dutiyajavanādīnaṃ anantarasamanantaraanantarūpanissayāsevananatthivigatapaccayehi, yaṃkiñci akusalaṃ karontassa hetu sahajāta aññamañña nissaya sampayutta atthi avigatapaccayehīti anekadhā paccayo hoti.

‘For the others, however, in many ways’ means it is a condition for demeritorious formations in many ways. How? For when greed and so on arise taking ignorance as object, it is a condition by way of object condition. When one esteems and enjoys it, it is by way of object-dominance and object-decisive-support conditions. For one who is deluded by ignorance, not seeing the danger, and commits the destruction of life and so on, it is by way of decisive support condition. For the second impulsion and so on, it is by way of contiguity, immediate contiguity, immediate decisive support, repetition, absence, and disappearance conditions. For one performing any unwholesome action, it is by way of root, co-nascence, mutuality, support, association, presence, and non-disappearance conditions. In these many ways it is a condition.

Pacchimānaṃ sā ekadhā paccayo matāti āneñjābhisaṅkhārānaṃ upanissayapaccayeneva ekadhā paccayo matā. So panassā upanissayabhāvo puññābhisaṅkhāre vuttanayeneva veditabboti.

‘For the final ones, that ignorance is considered a condition in one way’ means it is considered a condition for the imperturbable formations in one way only: by way of decisive support condition. And its nature as a decisive support should be understood in the same way as was stated for the meritorious formations.

617. Etthāha – kiṃ panāyamekāva avijjā saṅkhārānaṃ paccayo, udāhu aññepi paccayā [V 2.0171] santīti? Kiṃ panettha, yadi tāva ekāva, ekakāraṇavādo āpajjati. Athaññepi santi, “avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā”ti ekakāraṇaniddeso nupapajjatīti? Na nupapajjati. Kasmā? Yasmā –

617. Here one objects: ‘Is this ignorance the sole condition for formations, or do other conditions also exist?’ What is to be said on this? If, in the first place, it is the sole condition, the theory of a single cause follows. But if other conditions also exist, the specification of a single cause in ‘with ignorance as condition, formations’ is untenable.’ It is not untenable. Why? Because:

Ekaṃ na ekato idha, nānekamanekatopi no ekaṃ;

Phalamatthi atthi pana eka-hetuphaladīpane attho.

Here, a single result does not arise from a single cause, nor does a manifold one. Nor from many causes does a single result arise. A result does exist; however, there is a purpose in the explanation of a single cause and a single result.

Ekato [M 2.0174] hi kāraṇato na idha kiñci ekaṃ phalamatthi, na anekaṃ. Nāpi anekehi kāraṇehi ekaṃ. Anekehi pana kāraṇehi anekameva hoti. Tathā hi anekehi utupathavībījasalilasaṅkhātehi kāraṇehi anekameva rūpagandharasādikaṃ aṅkurasaṅkhātaṃ phalaṃ uppajjamānaṃ dissati. Yaṃ panetaṃ “avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇa”nti ekekahetuphaladīpanaṃ kataṃ, tattha attho atthi, payojanaṃ vijjati.

For, from a single cause, no single result whatsoever exists here, nor a manifold one. Nor from many causes is there a single result. But from many causes, there is indeed a manifold result. Thus, from many causes—namely, season, earth, seed, and water—a manifold result, the sprout, comprising form, smell, taste, and so on, is seen to arise. However, in that explanation of a single cause and a single result which is made, such as ‘With ignorance as condition, formations; with formations as condition, consciousness,’ there is a meaning, there is a purpose.

Bhagavā hi katthaci padhānattā, katthaci pākaṭattā, katthaci asādhāraṇattā desanāvilāsassa ca veneyyānañca anurūpato ekameva hetuṃ vā phalaṃ vā dīpeti. “Phassapaccayā vedanā”ti hi padhānattā ekameva hetuphalamāha. Phasso hi vedanāya padhānahetu yathāphassaṃ vedanā vavatthānato. Vedanā ca phassassa padhānaphalaṃ yathāvedanaṃ phassavavatthānato. “Semhasamuṭṭhānā ābādhā”ti (a. ni. 10.60) pākaṭattā ekaṃ hetumāha. Pākaṭo hi ettha semho, na kammādayo. “Ye keci, bhikkhave, akusalā dhammā, sabbe te ayonisomanasikāramūlakā”ti asādhāraṇattā ekaṃ hetumāha. Asādhāraṇo hi ayonisomanasikāro akusalānaṃ, sādhāraṇāni vatthārammaṇādīnīti. Tasmā ayamidha avijjā vijjamānesupi aññesu vatthārammaṇasahajātadhammādīsu saṅkhārakāraṇesu “assādānupassino taṇhā pavaḍḍhatī”ti (saṃ. ni. 2.52) ca “avijjāsamudayā āsavasamudayo”ti (ma. ni. 1.104) ca vacanato aññesampi taṇhādīnaṃ saṅkhārahetūnaṃ hetūti padhānattā, “avidvā, bhikkhave, avijjāgato puññābhisaṅkhārampi abhisaṅkharotī”ti pākaṭattā, asādhāraṇattā ca saṅkhārānaṃ hetubhāvena dīpitāti veditabbā. Eteneva ca ekekahetuphaladīpanaparihāravacanena sabbattha ekekahetuphaladīpane payojanaṃ veditabbanti.

For the Blessed One reveals a single cause or a single result, sometimes due to its prominence, sometimes due to its obviousness, sometimes due to its uniqueness, and in accordance with the elegance of the teaching and the suitability for the disciples. For in the statement, 'From contact as condition, feeling comes to be,' a single cause and result is stated due to prominence. Indeed, contact is the principal cause of feeling, as feeling is established in accordance with contact; and feeling is the principal result of contact, as contact is established in accordance with feeling. In 'Ailments that arise from phlegm,' a single cause is stated due to its obviousness. For here, phlegm is obvious, not kamma and so forth. In 'Monks, whatever unwholesome states there are, all have their root in unwise attention,' a single cause is stated due to its uniqueness. For unwise attention is unique to unwholesome states, whereas bases, objects, and so forth are common. Therefore, here, this ignorance is to be understood as having been revealed as the cause of formations—even though other causes for formations exist, such as bases, objects, co-nascent phenomena, and so forth—due to its prominence, as it is the cause of other causes of formations such as craving (according to the statements, 'For one who constantly sees gratification, craving increases,' and 'From the arising of ignorance comes the arising of the taints'); due to its obviousness (as stated in, 'Monks, an uninstructed person, affected by ignorance, generates even a meritorious formation'); and due to its uniqueness. And by this very explanation for revealing a single cause and result, the purpose in revealing a single cause and result in every instance should be understood.

618. Etthāha [V 2.0172] – evaṃ santepi ekantāniṭṭhaphalāya sāvajjāya avijjāya kathaṃ puññāneñjābhisaṅkhārapaccayattaṃ yujjati? Na hi nimbabījato ucchu uppajjatīti. Kathaṃ na yujjissati? Lokasmiñhi –

618. Here it is asked: 'Even so, how can ignorance, which is entirely undesirable in its result and blameworthy, be a condition for meritorious and imperturbable formations? For surely, sugarcane does not arise from a nimba seed.' How can it not be consistent? For in the world—

Viruddho [M 2.0175] cāviruddho ca, sadisāsadiso tathā;

Dhammānaṃ paccayo siddho, vipākā eva te ca na.

Opposed and unopposed, and likewise similar and dissimilar, a condition for phenomena is established; and those phenomena are not merely their results.

Dhammānaṃ hi ṭhānasabhāvakiccādiviruddho cāviruddho ca paccayo loke siddho. Purimacittaṃ hi aparacittassa ṭhānaviruddho paccayo, purimasippādisikkhā ca pacchā pavattamānānaṃ sippādikiriyānaṃ. Kammaṃ rūpassa sabhāvaviruddho paccayo, khīrādīni ca dadhiādīnaṃ. Āloko cakkhuviññāṇassa kiccaviruddho, guḷādayo ca āsavādīnaṃ. Cakkhurūpādayo pana cakkhuviññāṇādīnaṃ ṭhānāviruddhā paccayā. Purimajavanādayo pacchimajavanādīnaṃ sabhāvāviruddhā kiccāviruddhā ca.

For in the world, a condition for phenomena that is opposed and unopposed in terms of location, inherent nature, function, and so forth, is established. For the preceding mind is a condition opposed in location to the subsequent mind, and previous training in skills and so forth is a condition for the later performance of those skills. Kamma is a condition opposed in inherent nature to material form, and milk and so forth are conditions for curd and so forth. Light is a condition opposed in function to eye-consciousness, and molasses and so forth are conditions for intoxicants and so forth. However, the eye, visible forms, and so forth are conditions unopposed in location to eye-consciousness and so forth. The preceding impulsions and so forth are conditions unopposed in inherent nature and function to the subsequent impulsions and so forth.

Yathā ca viruddhāviruddhā paccayā siddhā, evaṃ sadisāsadisāpi. Sadisameva hi utuāhārasaṅkhātaṃ rūpaṃ rūpassa paccayo, sālibījādīni ca sāliphalādīnaṃ. Asadisampi rūpaṃ arūpassa, arūpañca rūpassa paccayo hoti, golomāviloma-visāṇa-dadhitilapiṭṭhādīni ca dubbā-sarabhūtiṇakādīnaṃ. Yesañca dhammānaṃ te viruddhāviruddhasadisāsadisapaccayā, na te dhammā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ vipākā eva.

Just as opposed and unopposed conditions are established, so too are similar and dissimilar ones. For indeed, a similar material phenomenon, namely, temperature and nutriment, is a condition for a material phenomenon, just as rice seeds and so forth are conditions for rice fruits and so forth. A dissimilar material phenomenon is also a condition for an immaterial phenomenon, and an immaterial phenomenon is a condition for a material phenomenon, just as cow hair, goat hair, horns, curds, and sesame flour are conditions for dubbā grass, sarabhū grass, and so forth. And those phenomena for which these opposed, unopposed, similar, and dissimilar conditions apply are not merely the results of those phenomena.

Iti ayaṃ avijjā vipākavasena ekantāniṭṭhaphalā, sabhāvavasena ca sāvajjāpi samānā sabbesampi etesaṃ puññābhisaṅkhārādīnaṃ yathānurūpaṃ ṭhānakiccasabhāvaviruddhāviruddhapaccayavasena, sadisāsadisapaccayavasena ca paccayo hotīti veditabbā. So cassā paccayabhāvo “yassa hi dukkhādīsu avijjāsaṅkhātaṃ aññāṇaṃ appahīnaṃ hoti, so dukkhe tāva pubbantādīsu ca aññāṇena saṃsāradukkhaṃ sukhasaññāya gahetvā tassa hetubhūte tividhepi saṅkhāre ārabhatī”tiādinā nayena vutto eva.

Thus, this ignorance, although being entirely undesirable in its result by way of its fruit and blameworthy by way of its inherent nature, is to be understood as a condition for all these meritorious formations and so forth, according to their respective suitability, by way of opposed and unopposed conditions in terms of location, function, and inherent nature, and by way of similar and dissimilar conditions. And its conditionality has been explained in the manner beginning with: 'For one for whom the unknowing called ignorance regarding suffering and so forth is not abandoned, that person, through unknowing regarding suffering, the past, and so forth, having grasped the suffering of saṃsāra with the perception of happiness, undertakes the threefold formations which are its cause.'

619. Apica ayaṃ aññopi pariyāyo –

619. Moreover, there is also this other method:

Cutūpapāte [V 2.0173] saṃsāre, saṅkhārānañca lakkhaṇe;

Yo paṭiccasamuppanna-dhammesu ca vimuyhati.

One who is bewildered about passing away and reappearing, about the cycle of existence, about the characteristics of formations, and about dependently arisen phenomena;

Abhisaṅkharoti so ete, saṅkhāre tividhe yato;

Avijjā paccayo tesaṃ, tividhānampayaṃ tatoti.

Because he fabricates these threefold formations, therefore this ignorance is the condition for those threefold formations.

Kathaṃ [M 2.0176] pana yo etesu vimuyhati, so tividhepete saṅkhāre karotīti ce. Cutiyā tāva vimūḷho “sabbattha khandhānaṃ bhedo maraṇa”nti cutiṃ agaṇhanto “satto marati, sattassa dehantarasaṅkamana”ntiādīni vikappeti.

If it is asked, 'How then does one who is bewildered about these things make these threefold formations?' First, being bewildered about passing away, not grasping passing away as 'the breaking up of the aggregates everywhere,' one speculates thus: 'A being dies, a being transmigrates to another body,' and so forth.

Upapāte vimūḷho “sabbattha khandhānaṃ pātubhāvo jātī”ti upapātaṃ agaṇhanto “satto upapajjati, sattassa navasarīrapātubhāvo”tiādīni vikappeti.

Being bewildered about reappearing, not grasping reappearing as 'the manifestation of aggregates everywhere is birth,' he speculates thus: 'A being reappears, there is the manifestation of a new body for a being,' and so forth.

Saṃsāre vimūḷho yo esa,

One who is bewildered about the cycle of existence—

“Khandhānañca paṭipāṭi, dhātuāyatanāna ca;

Abbocchinnaṃ vattamānā, saṃsāroti pavuccatī”ti. –

The uninterrupted, ongoing sequence of aggregates, and of elements and sense bases, is called the cycle of existence.

Evaṃ vaṇṇito saṃsāro, taṃ evaṃ agaṇhanto “ayaṃ satto asmā lokā paraṃ lokaṃ gacchati, parasmā lokā imaṃ lokaṃ āgacchatī”tiādīni vikappeti.

Not grasping the cycle of existence which is described thus, one speculates thus: 'This being goes from this world to the other world, and from the other world comes to this world,' and so forth.

Saṅkhārānaṃ lakkhaṇe vimūḷho saṅkhārānaṃ sabhāvalakkhaṇaṃ sāmaññalakkhaṇañca agaṇhanto saṅkhāre attato attaniyato dhuvato sukhato subhato vikappeti.

Being bewildered about the characteristics of formations, not grasping the specific and general characteristics of formations, one speculates about formations as self, as belonging to self, as permanent, as pleasant, and as beautiful.

Paṭiccasamuppannadhammesu vimūḷho avijjādīhi saṅkhārādīnaṃ pavattiṃ agaṇhanto “attā jānāti vā na jānāti vā, so eva karoti ca kāreti ca. So paṭisandhiyaṃ upapajjati, tassa aṇuissarādayo kalalādibhāvena sarīraṃ saṇṭhapento indriyāni sampādenti. So indriyasampanno phusati, vediyati, taṇhīyati, upādiyati, ghaṭiyati. So puna bhavantare bhavatī”ti [V 2.0174] vā, “sabbe sattā niyatisaṅgatibhāvapariṇatā”ti (dī. ni. 1.168) vā vikappeti.

Deluded concerning dependently arisen phenomena, not grasping the occurrence of formations and so on due to ignorance and so on, one speculates: 'The self either knows or does not know; it is that very self that acts and causes others to act. It takes rebirth, and atoms, a supreme being, and so on establish its body in the state of an embryo and the like, and develop its faculties. Endowed with faculties, it makes contact, feels, craves, clings, and strives. It is reborn again in another existence,' or 'All beings are transformed by destiny, association, and inherent nature' (Dī. Ni. 1.168).

So avijjāya andhīkato evaṃ vikappento yathā nāma andho pathaviyaṃ vicaranto maggampi amaggampi thalampi ninnampi samampi visamampi paṭipajjati, evaṃ puññampi apuññampi āneñjābhisaṅkhārampi abhisaṅkharotīti.

Blinded by ignorance, one speculates thus. Just as a blind person wandering on the ground may tread on a path or no path, on high ground or low ground, on even or uneven ground, so too does one generate meritorious, demeritorious, and imperturbable formations.

Tenetaṃ vuccati –

Therefore, this is said:

“Yathāpi [M 2.0177] nāma jaccandho, naro apariṇāyako;

Ekadā yāti maggena, ummaggenāpi ekadā.

“Just as a person born blind, without a guide, sometimes goes by the path, and sometimes by a wrong path;

“Saṃsāre saṃsaraṃ bālo, tathā apariṇāyako;

Karoti ekadā puññaṃ, apuññamapi ekadā.

“So too the fool, wandering in saṃsāra without a guide, sometimes does merit, and sometimes demerit.

“Yadā ca ñatvā so dhammaṃ, saccāni abhisamessati;

Tadā avijjūpasamā, upasanto carissatī”ti.

“But when, having known the Dhamma, one fully comprehends the Truths, then, with the stilling of ignorance, one will fare on, pacified.”

Ayaṃ “avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā”ti padasmiṃ vitthārakathā.

This is the detailed explanation of the phrase 'With ignorance as condition, formations arise.'

Saṅkhārapaccayāviññāṇapadavitthārakathā

The Detailed Explanation of the Phrase 'With Formations as Condition, Consciousness'

620. Saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇapade – viññāṇanti cakkhuviññāṇādi chabbidhaṃ. Tattha cakkhuviññāṇaṃ kusalavipākaṃ akusalavipākanti duvidhaṃ hoti. Tathā sotaghānajivhākaāyaviññāṇāni. Manoviññāṇaṃ kusalākusalavipākā dve manodhātuyo, tisso ahetukamanoviññāṇadhātuyo, aṭṭha sahetukāni kāmāvacaravipākacittāni, pañca rūpāvacarāni, cattāri arūpāvacarānīti bāvīsatividhaṃ hoti. Iti imehi chahi viññāṇehi sabbānipi bāttiṃsa lokiyavipākaviññāṇāni [V 2.0175] saṅgahitāni honti. Lokuttarāni pana vaṭṭakathāya na yujjantīti na gahitāni.

620. In the phrase 'With formations as condition, consciousness,' consciousness is sixfold, beginning with eye-consciousness. Among these, eye-consciousness is twofold: wholesome-resultant and unwholesome-resultant. Likewise for ear-, nose-, tongue-, and body-consciousness. Mind-consciousness is of twenty-two kinds: the two mind-elements that are wholesome- and unwholesome-resultant, the three rootless mind-consciousness-elements, the eight sense-sphere resultant consciousnesses with roots, the five form-sphere resultants, and the four formless-sphere resultants. Thus, by these six kinds of consciousness, all thirty-two mundane resultant consciousnesses are included. The supramundane ones, however, are not included as they are not appropriate to the discussion of the round of existence.

Tattha siyā “kathaṃ panetaṃ jānitabbaṃ idaṃ vuttappakāraṃ viññāṇaṃ saṅkhārapaccayā hotī”ti? Upacitakammābhāve vipākābhāvato. Vipākaṃ hetaṃ, vipākañca na upacitakammābhāve uppajjati. Yadi uppajjeyya sabbesaṃ sabbavipākāni uppajjeyyuṃ, na ca uppajjantīti jānitabbametaṃ saṅkhārapaccayā idaṃ viññāṇaṃ hotīti.

Herein, it might be asked: 'But how is it to be known that this consciousness, of the kind described, arises with formations as its condition?' It is to be known from the absence of a result in the absence of accumulated kamma. For this is a result, and a result does not arise in the absence of accumulated kamma. If it were to arise, all results would arise for all beings, but they do not. Therefore, it should be known that this consciousness arises with formations as its condition.

Katarasaṅkhārapaccayā kataraṃ viññāṇanti ce. Kāmāvacarapuññābhisaṅkhārapaccayā tāva kusalavipākāni pañca cakkhuviññāṇādīni, manoviññāṇe ekā manodhātu, dve manoviññāṇadhātuyo, aṭṭha kāmāvacaramahāvipākānīti soḷasa. Yathāha –

If it is asked, 'With which formation as condition does which consciousness arise?': Firstly, with meritorious formations of the sense sphere as condition, sixteen kinds of wholesome-resultant consciousness arise: the five beginning with eye-consciousness, and within mind-consciousness, one mind-element, two mind-consciousness-elements, and the eight great sense-sphere resultants. As it is said:

“Kāmāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa kaṭattā upacitattā vipākaṃ cakkhuviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti… sota… ghāna… jivhā… kāyaviññāṇaṃ [M 2.0178]… vipākā manodhātu uppannā hoti. Somanassasahagatā manoviññāṇadhātu uppannā hoti. Upekkhāsahagatā manoviññāṇadhātu uppannā hoti. Somanassasahagatā ñāṇasampayuttā. Somanassasahagatā ñāṇasampayuttā sasaṅkhārena. Somanassasahagatā ñāṇavippayuttā. Somanassasahagatā ñāṇavippayuttā sasaṅkhārena. Upekkhāsahagatā ñāṇasampayuttā. Upekkhāsahagatā ñāṇasampayuttā sasaṅkhārena. Upekkhāsahagatā ñāṇavippayuttā. Upekkhāsahagatā ñāṇavippayuttā sasaṅkhārenā”ti (dha. sa. 431, 498).

“Due to the performance and accumulation of wholesome kamma pertaining to the sense sphere, resultant eye-consciousness arises… ear-consciousness… nose-consciousness… tongue-consciousness… body-consciousness… a resultant mind-element arises. A mind-consciousness-element accompanied by joy arises. A mind-consciousness-element accompanied by equanimity arises. A mind-consciousness-element accompanied by joy and associated with knowledge arises. A mind-consciousness-element accompanied by joy, associated with knowledge, and prompted arises. A mind-consciousness-element accompanied by joy and dissociated from knowledge arises. A mind-consciousness-element accompanied by joy, dissociated from knowledge, and prompted arises. A mind-consciousness-element accompanied by equanimity and associated with knowledge arises. A mind-consciousness-element accompanied by equanimity, associated with knowledge, and prompted arises. A mind-consciousness-element accompanied by equanimity and dissociated from knowledge arises. A mind-consciousness-element accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge, and prompted arises.”

Rūpāvacarapuññābhisaṅkhārapaccayā pana pañca rūpāvacaravipākāni. Yathāha –

Furthermore, with meritorious formations of the form sphere as condition, five form-sphere resultants arise. As it is said:

“Tasseva rūpāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa kaṭattā upacitattā vipākaṃ vivicceva kāmehi paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… pañcamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharatī”ti (dha. sa. 499). Evaṃ puññābhisaṅkhārapaccayā ekavīsatividhaṃ viññāṇaṃ hoti.

“Due to the performance and accumulation of that same wholesome kamma pertaining to the form sphere, as a result, being quite secluded from sensual pleasures… one attains and abides in the first jhāna… up to… the fifth jhāna.” Thus, with meritorious formations as condition, consciousness of twenty-one kinds arises.

Apuññābhisaṅkhārapaccayā [V 2.0176] pana akusalavipākāni pañca cakkhuviññāṇādīni, ekā manodhātu, ekā manoviññāṇadhātūti evaṃ sattavidhaṃ viññāṇaṃ hoti. Yathāha –

Furthermore, with demeritorious formations as condition, seven kinds of unwholesome-resultant consciousness arise: the five beginning with eye-consciousness, one mind-element, and one mind-consciousness-element. As it is said:

“Akusalassa kammassa kaṭattā upacitattā vipākaṃ cakkhuviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti… sota… ghāna… jivhā… kāyaviññāṇaṃ… vipākā manodhātu vipākā manoviññāṇadhātu uppannā hotī”ti (dha. sa. 556).

“Due to the performance and accumulation of unwholesome kamma, resultant eye-consciousness arises… ear-consciousness… nose-consciousness… tongue-consciousness… body-consciousness… a resultant mind-element arises; a resultant mind-consciousness-element arises.”

Āneñjābhisaṅkhārapaccayā pana cattāri arūpavipākānīti evaṃ catubbidhaṃ viññāṇaṃ hoti. Yathāha –

Furthermore, with imperturbable formations as condition, four formless resultants arise; thus, consciousness is fourfold. As it is said:

“Tasseva arūpāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa kaṭattā upacitattā vipākaṃ sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā ākāsānañcāyatanasaññāsahagataṃ…pe… viññāṇañcā…pe… ākiñcaññā…pe… nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasahagataṃ sukhassa ca dukkhassa ca pahānā catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharatī”ti (dha. sa. 501).

“Due to the performance and accumulation of that same wholesome kamma pertaining to the formless sphere, as a result, with the complete surmounting of all perceptions of form… and through the abandoning of pleasure and pain, one attains and abides in the fourth jhāna accompanied by the perception of the base of infinite space… up to… the fourth jhāna accompanied by the perception of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.”

621. Evaṃ [M 2.0179] yaṃ saṅkhārapaccayā yaṃ viññāṇaṃ hoti, taṃ ñatvā idānissa evaṃ pavatti veditabbā – sabbameva hi idaṃ pavattipaṭisandhivasena dvedhā pavattati. Tattha dve pañcaviññāṇāni, dve manodhātuyo, somanassasahagatā ahetukamanoviññāṇadhātūti imāni terasa pañcavokārabhave pavattiyaññeva pavattanti. Sesāni ekūnavīsati tīsu bhavesu yathānurūpaṃ pavattiyampi paṭisandhiyampi pavattanti.

621. Thus, having known that whatever consciousness arises dependent on formations, its occurrence should now be understood as follows: Indeed, all this occurs in two ways—by way of the course of life and by way of rebirth-linking. Herein, the two sets of five-door consciousness, the two mind-elements, and the joy-accompanied rootless mind-consciousness-element—these thirteen occur only in the five-constituent existence and only during the course of life. The remaining nineteen occur in the three existences, as is appropriate, both during the course of life and at rebirth-linking.

Kathaṃ? Kusalavipākāni tāva cakkhuviññāṇādīni pañca kusalavipākena akusalavipākena vā nibbattassa yathākkamaṃ paripākaṃ upagatindriyassa cakkhādīnaṃ āpāthagataṃ iṭṭhaṃ iṭṭhamajjhattaṃ vā rūpādiārammaṇaṃ ārabbha cakkhādipasādaṃ nissāya dassanasavanaghāyanasāyanaphusanakiccaṃ sādhayamānāni pavattanti. Tathā akusalavipākāni pañca. Kevalañhi tesaṃ aniṭṭhaṃ aniṭṭhamajjhattaṃ vā ārammaṇaṃ hoti. Ayameva viseso. Dasapi cetāni niyatadvārārammaṇavatthuṭṭhānāni niyatakiccāneva ca bhavanti.

How so? Firstly, for one who has been reborn through a wholesome or unwholesome resultant consciousness and whose faculties have matured in due course, the five wholesome-resultant consciousnesses, beginning with eye-consciousness, arise. They do so by taking as object a desirable or moderately desirable visible form, etc., that has come into the range of the eye, etc., and by depending on the eye-sensitivity, etc., thereby accomplishing the functions of seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting, and touching. The five unwholesome-resultant consciousnesses arise similarly. For them, however, the object is exclusively undesirable or moderately undesirable. This alone is the difference. And these ten have fixed doors, objects, bases, and locations, and they have only fixed functions.

Tato [V 2.0177] kusalavipākānaṃ cakkhuviññāṇādīnaṃ anantarā kusalavipākā manodhātu tesaṃyeva ārammaṇaṃ ārabbha hadayavatthuṃ nissāya sampaṭicchanakiccaṃ sādhayamānā pavattati. Tathā akusalavipākānaṃ anantarā akusalavipākā. Idañca pana dvayaṃ aniyatadvārārammaṇaṃ niyatavatthuṭṭhānaṃ niyatakiccañca hoti.

Then, immediately following the wholesome-resultant consciousnesses beginning with eye-consciousness, the wholesome-resultant mind-element arises, accomplishing the function of receiving by taking their very same object and depending on the heart-base. Similarly, the unwholesome-resultant mind-element arises immediately following the unwholesome-resultant consciousnesses. This pair, however, has an unfixed door and object, a fixed base and location, and a fixed function.

Somanassasahagatā pana ahetukamanoviññāṇadhātu kusalavipākamanodhātuyā anantarā tassā eva ārammaṇaṃ ārabbha hadayavatthuṃ nissāya santīraṇakiccaṃ sādhayamānā chasu dvāresu balavārammaṇe kāmāvacarasattānaṃ yebhuyyena lobhasampayuttajavanāvasāne bhavaṅgavīthiṃ pacchinditvā javanena gahitārammaṇe tadārammaṇavasena ca sakiṃ vā dvikkhattuṃ vā pavattatīti majjhimaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ. Abhidhammaṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana tadārammaṇe dve cittavārā āgatā. Idaṃ pana cittaṃ tadārammaṇanti ca piṭṭhibhavaṅganti cāti dve nāmāni labhati. Aniyatadvārārammaṇaṃ niyatavatthukaṃ aniyataṭṭhānakiccañca hotīti. Evaṃ tāva terasa pañcavokārabhave pavattiyaññeva pavattantīti veditabbāni.

Furthermore, the rootless mind-consciousness-element accompanied by joy, immediately following the wholesome-resultant mind-element, accomplishes the function of investigating by taking that very same object and depending on the heart-base; and, at the six doors, when the object is strong, for sense-sphere beings, it occurs mostly at the end of greed-accompanied impulsion, after cutting off the stream of the life-continuum, once or twice by way of registration in regard to the object taken by the impulsion. So it is said in the Majjhima Commentary. In the Abhidhamma Commentary, however, two thought-moments are given for registration. This consciousness, moreover, obtains two names: 'registration' and 'posterior life-continuum.' It has an unfixed door and object, a fixed base, and an unfixed location and function. Thus, it should be known that these thirteen consciousnesses occur only in the five-constituent existence and only during the course of life.

Sesesu [M 2.0180] ekūnavīsatiyā na kiñci attano anurūpāya paṭisandhiyā na pavattati. Pavattiyaṃ pana kusalākusalavipākā tāva dve ahetukamanoviññāṇadhātuyo pañcadvāre kusalākusalavipākamanodhātūnaṃ anantarā santīraṇakiccaṃ, chasu dvāresu pubbe vuttanayeneva tadārammaṇakiccaṃ, attanā dinnapaṭisandhito uddhaṃ asati bhavaṅgupacchedake cittuppāde bhavaṅgakiccaṃ, ante cutikiccañcāti cattāri kiccāni sādhayamānā niyatavatthukā aniyatadvārārammaṇaṭṭhānakiccā hutvā pavattanti.

Among the remaining nineteen, there is not one that does not occur with a rebirth-linking appropriate to itself. During the course of life, however, the two rootless mind-consciousness-elements—which are wholesome and unwholesome resultants—arise accomplishing four functions: at the five doors, immediately following the wholesome and unwholesome resultant mind-elements, the function of investigating; at the six doors, in the way previously stated, the function of registration; after the rebirth-linking given by themselves, when there is no arising of consciousness that cuts off the life-continuum, the function of life-continuum; and at the end, the function of death. They occur having a fixed base, and having an unfixed door, object, location, and function.

Aṭṭha kāmāvacarasahetukacittāni vuttanayeneva chasu dvāresu tadārammaṇakiccaṃ, attanā dinnapaṭisandhito uddhaṃ asati bhavaṅgupacchedake cittuppāde bhavaṅgakiccaṃ, ante cutikiccañcāti tīṇi kiccāni sādhayamānāni niyatavatthukāni aniyatadvārārammaṇaṭṭhānakiccāni hutvā pavattanti.

The eight root-accompanied sense-sphere resultant consciousnesses, in the way already stated, arise accomplishing three functions: at the six doors, the function of registration; after the rebirth-linking given by themselves, when there is no arising of consciousness that cuts off the life-continuum, the function of life-continuum; and at the end, the function of death. They occur having a fixed base, and having an unfixed door, object, location, and function.

Pañca rūpāvacarāni cattāri ca āruppāni attanā dinnapaṭisandhito uddhaṃ asati bhavaṅgupacchedake cittuppāde bhavaṅgakiccaṃ, ante cutikiccañcāti kiccadvayaṃ sādhayamānāni pavattanti[V 2.0178]. Tesu rūpāvacarāni niyatavatthārammaṇāni aniyataṭṭhānakiccāni, itarāni niyatavatthukāni niyatārammaṇāni aniyataṭṭhānakiccāni hutvā pavattantīti evaṃ tāva bāttiṃsavidhampi viññāṇaṃ pavattiyaṃ saṅkhārapaccayā pavattati. Tatrāssa te te saṅkhārā kammapaccayena ca upanissayapaccayena ca paccayā honti.

The five fine-material-sphere and four formless-sphere resultant consciousnesses arise accomplishing a pair of functions: after the rebirth-linking given by themselves, when there is no arising of consciousness that cuts off the life-continuum, the function of life-continuum; and at the end, the function of death. Among them, the fine-material-sphere consciousnesses have a fixed base and object, and an unfixed location and function. The others, having no fixed base, have a fixed object, and an unfixed location and function. Thus, during the course of life, the thirty-two-fold resultant consciousness arises dependent on formations. Therein, for that consciousness, those various formations are conditions by way of kamma condition and by way of decisive support condition.

622. Yaṃ pana vuttaṃ “sesesu ekūnavīsatiyā na kiñci attano anurūpāya paṭisandhiyā na pavattatī”ti, taṃ atisaṃkhittattā dubbijānaṃ. Tenassa vitthāranayadassanatthaṃ vuccati – kati paṭisandhiyo, kati paṭisandhicittāni, kena kattha paṭisandhi hoti, kiṃ paṭisandhiyā ārammaṇanti?

622. But the statement that was made, 'Among the remaining nineteen, there is not one that does not occur with a rebirth-linking appropriate to itself,' is difficult to understand because it is too concise. Therefore, to show the detailed method for this, it is asked: How many kinds of rebirth-linking are there? How many rebirth-linking consciousnesses are there? By what consciousness and where does rebirth-linking occur? What is the object of rebirth-linking?

Asaññapaṭisandhiyā saddhiṃ vīsati paṭisandhiyo. Vuttappakārāneva ekūnavīsati paṭisandhicittāni. Tattha akusalavipākāya ahetukamanoviññāṇadhātuyā apāyesu paṭisandhi hoti. Kusalavipākāya manussaloke jaccandhajātibadhirajātiummattakajātieḷamūganapuṃsakādīnaṃ. Aṭṭhahi sahetukakāmāvacaravipākehi kāmāvacaradevesu ceva manussesu ca puññavantānaṃ paṭisandhi hoti. Pañcahi rūpāvacaravipākehi rūpībrahmaloke. Catūhi arūpāvacaravipākehi arūpaloketi. Yena ca yattha paṭisandhi hoti[M 2.0181], sā eva tassa anurūpā paṭisandhi nāma. Saṅkhepato pana paṭisandhiyā tīṇi ārammaṇāni honti atītaṃ paccuppannaṃ navattabbañca. Asaññā paṭisandhi anārammaṇāti.

Together with the non-percipient rebirth-linking, there are twenty kinds of rebirth-linking. There are nineteen rebirth-linking consciousnesses, of the types already described. Among them, through the unwholesome-resultant rootless mind-consciousness-element, rebirth-linking occurs in the woeful states. Through the wholesome-resultant one, rebirth-linking occurs in the human world for those born blind, born deaf, born insane, born idiotic and mute, for hermaphrodites, and so forth. Through the eight root-accompanied sense-sphere resultant consciousnesses, rebirth-linking occurs for meritorious beings in the sense-sphere celestial worlds and among humans. Through the five fine-material-sphere resultant consciousnesses, it occurs in the fine-material Brahmā world. Through the four formless-sphere resultant consciousnesses, it occurs in the formless world. And by whichever consciousness and in whichever existence rebirth-linking occurs, that very one is called the rebirth-linking appropriate to it. In brief, however, there are three kinds of objects for rebirth-linking: past, present, and that which is not to be spoken of. The non-percipient rebirth-linking is without an object.

Tattha viññāṇañcāyatananevasaññānāsaññāyatanapaṭisandhīnaṃ atītameva ārammaṇaṃ. Dasannaṃ kāmāvacarānaṃ atītaṃ vā paccuppannaṃ vā. Sesānaṃ navattabbameva. Evaṃ tīsu ārammaṇesu pavattamānā pana paṭisandhi yasmā atītārammaṇassa vā navattabbārammaṇassa vā cuticittassa anantarameva pavattati. Paccuppannārammaṇaṃ pana cuticittaṃ nāma natthi. Tasmā dvīsu ārammaṇesu aññatarārammaṇāya cutiyā anantarā tīsu ārammaṇesu aññatarārammaṇāya paṭisandhiyā sugatiduggativasena pavattanākāro veditabbo.

Among these, for the rebirth-linkings of the base of infinite consciousness and the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, the object is only past. For the ten sense-sphere rebirth-linkings, the object is either past or present. For the rest, it is only a concept. Now, since the rebirth-linking that occurs with one of these three objects arises immediately after a death-consciousness that has either a past object or a conceptual object—and there is no such thing as a death-consciousness with a present object—therefore, the manner of occurrence of a rebirth-linking with one of the three objects, immediately after a death with one of the two objects, by way of a fortunate or unfortunate destiny, should be understood.

623. Seyyathidaṃ – kāmāvacarasugatiyaṃ tāva ṭhitassa pāpakammino puggalassa “tānissa tasmiṃ samaye olambantī”tiādivacanato (ma. ni. 3.248) maraṇamañce nipannassa [V 2.0179] yathūpacitaṃ pāpakammaṃ vā kammanimittaṃ vā manodvāre āpāthamāgacchati. Taṃ ārabbha uppannāya tadārammaṇapariyosānāya javanavīthiyā anantaraṃ bhavaṅgavisayaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā cuticittaṃ uppajjati. Tasmiṃ niruddhe tadeva āpāthagataṃ kammaṃ vā kammanimittaṃ vā ārabbha anupacchinnakilesabalavināmitaṃ duggatipariyāpannaṃ paṭisandhicittaṃ uppajjati. Ayaṃ atītārammaṇāya cutiyā anantarā atītārammaṇā paṭisandhi.

623. To explain: for a person of unwholesome kamma who is established in a fortunate sense-sphere destiny, in accordance with the saying, “At that time, they hang over him,” when lying on the deathbed, the accumulated unwholesome kamma or a kamma-sign comes into the range of the mind-door. Taking that as object, a javana process culminating in registering arises, and immediately after that, the death-consciousness arises, having taken the object of the life-continuum as its object. When that has ceased, the rebirth-linking consciousness arises, taking that very kamma or kamma-sign that came into range as its object, inclined by the power of the uncut defilements, and included in a woeful destiny. This is a rebirth-linking with a past object immediately following a death with a past object.

Aparassa maraṇasamaye vuttappakārakammavasena narakādīsu aggijālavaṇṇādikaṃ duggatinimittaṃ manodvāre āpāthamāgacchati, tassa dvikkhattuṃ bhavaṅge uppajjitvā niruddhe taṃ ārammaṇaṃ ārabbha ekaṃ āvajjanaṃ, maraṇassa āsannabhāvena mandībhūtavegattā pañca javanāni, dve tadārammaṇānīti tīṇi vīthicittāni uppajjanti. Tato bhavaṅgavisayaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā ekaṃ cuticittaṃ. Ettāvatā ekādasa cittakkhaṇā atītā honti. Athassa avasesapañcacittakkhaṇāyuke tasmiññeva ārammaṇe paṭisandhicittaṃ uppajjati. Ayaṃ atītārammaṇāya cutiyā anantarā paccuppannārammaṇā paṭisandhi.

For another person at the time of death, by the power of kamma of the aforementioned kind, a sign of a woeful destiny, such as the appearance of flames in hell and so forth, comes into the range of the mind-door. For that person, after two life-continuum moments have arisen and ceased, taking that object, one adverting consciousness, five impulsion moments—their force weakened due to the proximity of death—and two registering moments arise; thus three kinds of process-consciousnesses arise. Then, one death-consciousness arises, having taken the object of the life-continuum as its object. By this much, eleven mind-moments have passed. Then, for that person, when that same object has a remaining lifespan of five mind-moments, the rebirth-linking consciousness arises. This is a rebirth-linking with a present object immediately following a death with a past object.

Aparassa [M 2.0182] maraṇasamaye pañcannaṃ dvārānaṃ aññatarasmiṃ rāgādihetubhūtaṃ hīnamārammaṇaṃ āpāthamāgacchati. Tassa yathākkamena uppanne voṭṭhabbanāvasāne maraṇassa āsannabhāvena mandībhūtavegattā pañca javanāni, dve tadārammaṇāni ca uppajjanti. Tato bhavaṅgavisayaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā ekaṃ cuticittaṃ. Ettāvatā ca dve bhavaṅgāni, āvajjanaṃ, dassanaṃ, sampaṭicchanaṃ, santīraṇaṃ, voṭṭhabbanaṃ, pañca javanāni, dve tadārammaṇāni, ekaṃ cuticittanti pañcadasa cittakkhaṇā atītā honti. Athāvasesaekacittakkhaṇāyuke tasmiññeva ārammaṇe paṭisandhicittaṃ uppajjati. Ayampi atītārammaṇāya cutiyā anantarā paccuppannārammaṇā paṭisandhi. Esa tāva atītārammaṇāya sugaticutiyā anantarā atītapaccuppannārammaṇāya duggatipaṭisandhiyā pavattanākāro.

For another person at the time of death, a low object that is a cause for lust and so forth comes into the range of one of the five doors. For that person, after the process has occurred in due order up to the end of the determining stage, five impulsion moments—their force weakened due to the proximity of death—and two registering moments arise. Then, one death-consciousness arises, having taken the object of the life-continuum as its object. By this much, fifteen mind-moments have passed: two life-continuum moments, adverting, seeing, receiving, investigating, determining, five impulsions, two registering moments, and one death-consciousness. Then, when that same object has a remaining lifespan of one mind-moment, the rebirth-linking consciousness arises. This, too, is a rebirth-linking with a present object immediately following a death with a past object. This, then, is the manner of occurrence of a rebirth-linking into a woeful destiny with a past or present object, immediately following a death from a blissful destiny with a past object.

624. Duggatiyaṃ ṭhitassa pana upacitānavajjakammassa vuttanayeneva taṃ anavajjakammaṃ vā kammanimittaṃ vā manodvāre āpāthamāgacchatīti kaṇhapakkhe sukkapakkhaṃ ṭhapetvā sabbaṃ purimanayeneva veditabbaṃ. Ayaṃ atītārammaṇāya duggaticutiyā anantarā atītapaccuppannārammaṇāya sugatipaṭisandhiyā pavattanākāro.

624. For one established in a woeful destiny, however, who has accumulated blameless kamma, when that blameless kamma or its kamma-sign comes into the range of the mind-door in the aforementioned manner, everything should be understood in the same way as before, by substituting the bright side for the dark side. This is the manner of occurrence of a rebirth-linking into a blissful destiny with a past or present object, immediately following a death from a woeful destiny with a past object.

625. Sugatiyaṃ [V 2.0180] ṭhitassa pana upacitānavajjakammassa “tānissa tasmiṃ samaye olambantī”tiādivacanato maraṇamañce nipannassa yathūpacitaṃ anavajjakammaṃ vā kammanimittaṃ vā manodvāre āpāthamāgacchati. Tañca kho upacitakāmāvacarānavajjakammasseva. Upacitamahaggatakammassa pana kammanimittameva āpāthamāgacchati. Taṃ ārabbha uppannāya tadārammaṇapariyosānāya suddhāya vā javanavīthiyā anantaraṃ bhavaṅgavisayaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā cuticittaṃ uppajjati. Tasmiṃ niruddhe tameva āpāthagataṃ kammaṃ vā kammanimittaṃ vā ārabbha anupacchinnakilesabalavināmitaṃ sugatipariyāpannaṃ paṭisandhicittaṃ uppajjati. Ayaṃ atītārammaṇāya cutiyā anantarā atītārammaṇā vā navattabbārammaṇā vā paṭisandhi.

625. Furthermore, for one established in a blissful destiny who has accumulated blameless kamma, when lying on the deathbed, in accordance with the saying, “At that time, they hang over him,” the accumulated blameless kamma or a kamma-sign comes into the range of the mind-door. And this applies only to one with accumulated sense-sphere blameless kamma. For one with accumulated sublime kamma, however, only the kamma-sign comes into range. Taking that as object, a javana process arises that either culminates in registering or is a pure process. Immediately after that, the death-consciousness arises, having taken the object of the life-continuum as its object. When that has ceased, taking that very kamma or kamma-sign that came into range as its object, a rebirth-linking consciousness included in a blissful destiny arises, inclined by the power of the uncut defilements. This is a rebirth-linking with a past object or a conceptual object, immediately following a death with a past object.

Aparassa maraṇasamaye kāmāvacaraanavajjakammavasena manussaloke mātukucchivaṇṇasaṅkhātaṃ vā devaloke uyyānavimānakapparukkhādivaṇṇasaṅkhātaṃ vā sugatinimittaṃ manodvāre āpāthamāgacchati, tassa duggatinimitte [M 2.0183] dassitānukkameneva cuticittānantaraṃ paṭisandhicittaṃ uppajjati. Ayaṃ atītārammaṇāya cutiyā anantarā paccuppannārammaṇā paṭisandhi.

For another at the time of death, by the power of blameless sense-sphere kamma, a sign of a blissful destiny comes into the range of the mind-door, such as the sight of what is known as a mother’s womb in the human world, or the sight of what is known as a park, mansion, wish-fulfilling tree, and so forth in the deva world. For that person, the rebirth-linking consciousness arises immediately after the death-consciousness, following the very sequence shown in the case of the sign of a woeful destiny. This is a rebirth-linking with a present object immediately following a death with a past object.

Aparassa maraṇasamaye ñātakā “ayaṃ tāta tavatthāya buddhapūjā karīyati cittaṃ pasādehī”ti vatvā pupphadāmapaṭākādivasena rūpārammaṇaṃ vā, dhammassavanatūriyapūjādivasena saddārammaṇaṃ vā, dhūmavāsagandhādivasena gandhārammaṇaṃ vā, “idaṃ tāta sāyassu tavatthāya dātabbadeyyadhamma”nti vatvā madhuphāṇitādivasena rasārammaṇaṃ vā, “idaṃ tāta phusassu tavatthāya dātabbadeyyadhamma”nti vatvā cīnapaṭṭasomārapaṭṭādivasena phoṭṭhabbārammaṇaṃ vā pañcadvāre upasaṃharanti, tassa tasmiṃ āpāthagate rūpādiārammaṇe yathākkamena uppannavoṭṭhabbanāvasāne maraṇassa āsannabhāvena mandībhūtavegattā pañca javanāni, dve tadārammaṇāni ca uppajjanti. Tato bhavaṅgavisayaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā ekaṃ cuticittaṃ, tadavasāne tasmiññeva ekacittakkhaṇaṭṭhitike ārammaṇe paṭisandhicittaṃ uppajjati. Ayampi atītārammaṇāya cutiyā anantarā paccuppannārammaṇā paṭisandhi.

At the time of another's death, relatives say, "Dear one, this is being done for your sake—an offering to the Buddha. Please gladden your mind!" and present a sight-object through flowers, garlands, flags, and the like; or a sound-object through listening to the Dhamma, musical instrument offerings, and the like; or a smell-object through incense, perfumes, and the like; or saying, "Dear one, taste this—it is a gift to be given for your sake," they present a taste-object through honey, syrup, and the like; or saying, "Dear one, touch this—it is a gift to be given for your sake," they present a touch-object through Chinese silk, linen, and the like at the five sense-doors. When that sight-object, etc., enters the range of perception, due to the weakened force caused by the nearness of death, five impulsions and two registrations arise in sequence at the end of the determining phase. Then, making the life-continuum its object, one death-consciousness arises.
