At its cessation, rebirth-linking consciousness arises, taking as its object that very object which endured for a single mind-moment. This is also a rebirth-linking with a present object immediately following a death with a past object.

626. Aparassa pana pathavīkasiṇajjhānādivasena paṭiladdhamahaggatassa sugatiyaṃ ṭhitassa maraṇasamaye kāmāvacarakusalakamma-kammanimitta-gatinimittānaṃ vā aññataraṃ, pathavīkasiṇādikaṃ vā nimittaṃ, mahaggatacittaṃ vā manodvāre āpāthamāgacchati, cakkhusotānaṃ vā aññatarasmiṃ kusaluppattihetubhūtaṃ [V 2.0181] paṇītamārammaṇaṃ āpāthamāgacchati, tassa yathākkamena uppannavoṭṭhabbanāvasāne maraṇassa āsannabhāvena mandībhūtavegattā pañca javanāni uppajjanti. Mahaggatagatikānaṃ pana tadārammaṇaṃ natthi, tasmā javanānantaraṃyeva bhavaṅgavisayaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā ekaṃ cuticittaṃ uppajjati. Tassāvasāne kāmāvacaramahaggatasugatīnaṃ aññatarasugatipariyāpannaṃ yathūpaṭṭhitesu ārammaṇesu aññatarārammaṇaṃ paṭisandhicittaṃ uppajjati. Ayaṃ navattabbārammaṇāya sugaticutiyā anantarā atītapaccuppannanavattabbārammaṇānaṃ aññatarārammaṇā paṭisandhi.

626. For another being who has attained an exalted state through the earth kasiṇa jhāna or similar, and is established in a happy destination, at the time of death, one of the following appears in the mind-door: either a sense-sphere wholesome kamma, a kamma-sign, or a destination-sign; or the earth kasiṇa or similar sign; or an exalted consciousness. Alternatively, a refined object that serves as a cause for the arising of wholesome consciousness appears in either the eye- or ear-door. Following the arising of these in sequence, when the process of determining ends, due to the proximity of death and the weakened force of mental activity, five impulsions arise. But for those with a destination in the exalted realms, there is no registration. Therefore, immediately after the impulsions, making the life-continuum its object, a single death-consciousness arises. At its cessation, rebirth-linking consciousness arises, pertaining to one of the happy destinations, either the sense-sphere or exalted, taking as its object one of the objects that have appeared. This is a rebirth-linking that has as its object one of the past, present, or ineffable objects, immediately following a death in a happy destination that had an ineffable object.

Etenānusārena āruppacutiyāpi anantarā paṭisandhi veditabbā. Ayaṃ atītanavattabbārammaṇāya sugaticutiyā anantarā atītanavattabbapaccuppannārammaṇāya paṭisandhiyā pavattanākāro.

By this method, the rebirth immediately following a death in the formless realm should also be understood. This is the manner of occurrence for a rebirth with a past, ineffable, or present object, immediately following a death in a happy destination that had a past or ineffable object.

627. Duggatiyaṃ [M 2.0184] ṭhitassa pana pāpakammino vuttanayeneva taṃ kammaṃ kammanimittaṃ gatinimittaṃ vā manodvāre. Pañcadvāre vā pana akusaluppatti hetubhūtaṃ ārammaṇaṃ āpāthamāgacchati, athassa yathākkamena cuticittāvasāne duggatipariyāpannaṃ tesu ārammaṇesu aññatarārammaṇaṃ paṭisandhicittaṃ uppajjati. Ayaṃ atītārammaṇāya duggaticutiyā anantarā atītapaccuppannārammaṇāya paṭisandhiyā pavattanākāroti. Ettāvatā ekūnavīsatividhassāpi viññāṇassa paṭisandhivasena pavatti dīpitā hoti.

627. For an evil-doer established in a bad destination, in the manner previously described, that kamma, kamma-sign, or destination-sign appears at the mind-door. Or else, at the five sense-doors, an object that serves as the cause for the arising of unwholesome consciousness presents itself. Then, in due order, at the cessation of his death-consciousness, rebirth-linking consciousness arises taking as its object one of those objects pertaining to a bad destination. This is the manner of occurrence for a rebirth with a past or present object, immediately following a death in a bad destination that had a past object. Thus, the occurrence of the nineteen-fold consciousness by way of rebirth-linking has been explained.

628. Tayidaṃ sabbampi evaṃ,

628. All this is thus:

Pavattamānaṃ sandhimhi, dvedhā kammena vattati;

Missādīhi ca bhedehi, bhedassa duvidhādiko.

Occurring at the junction, it proceeds twofold by kamma; and by distinctions such as mixed, its division is twofold and so forth.

Idañhi ekūnavīsatividhampi vipākaviññāṇaṃ paṭisandhimhi pavattamānā dvedhā kammena vattati. Yathāsakañhi ekassa janakakammaṃ nānākkhaṇikakammapaccayena ceva upanissayapaccayena ca paccayo hoti. Vuttañhetaṃ “kusalākusalaṃ kammaṃ vipākassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo”ti (paṭṭhā. 1.1.423). Evaṃ vattamānassa panassa missādīhi bhedehi duvidhādikopi bhedo veditabbo.

This nineteenfold resultant consciousness, functioning at rebirth-linking, operates in two ways through kamma. For each, its own generative kamma serves as a condition both by way of being a different-moment kamma condition and by way of being a dependence condition. As it is said: "Wholesome and unwholesome kamma is a condition for its result by way of dependence condition" (Paṭṭhāna 1.1.423). Moreover, for this consciousness functioning thus, its twofold and other classifications should be understood through distinctions such as mixed, etc.

Seyyathidaṃ [V 2.0182] – idañhi paṭisandhivasena ekadhā pavattamānampi rūpena saha missāmissabhedato duvidhaṃ. Kāmarūpārūpabhavabhedato tividhaṃ. Aṇḍajajalābuja-saṃsedaja-opapātikayonivasena catubbidhaṃ. Gativasena pañcavidhaṃ. Viññāṇaṭṭhitivasena sattavidhaṃ. Sattāvāsavasena aṭṭhavidhaṃ hoti.

That is to say: though occurring as one by way of rebirth-linking, it is twofold by way of the distinction of being mixed and unmixed with matter. It is threefold by way of the distinction of sense-sphere, form, and formless existences. It is fourfold by way of the modes of birth: egg-born, womb-born, moisture-born, and spontaneously born. It is fivefold by way of destinations. It is sevenfold by way of the stations of consciousness. It is eightfold by way of the abodes of beings.

629. Tattha,

629. Therein,

Missaṃ dvidhā bhāvabhedā, sabhāvaṃ tattha ca dvidhā;

Dve vā tayo vā dasakā, omato ādinā saha.

The mixed is twofold by distinction of sex, and therein that with sex is also twofold; two or three decads, at the minimum, along with the initial consciousness.

Missaṃ dvidhā bhāvabhedāti yaṃ hetaṃ ettha aññatra arūpabhavā rūpamissaṃ paṭisandhiviññāṇaṃ uppajjati, taṃ rūpabhave itthindriyapurisindriyasaṅkhātena bhāvena vinā uppattito. Kāmabhave aññatra jātipaṇḍakapaṭisandhiyā bhāvena saha uppattito sa-bhāvaṃ, a-bhāvanti duvidhaṃ hoti.

As to 'The mixed is twofold by distinction of sex': that rebirth-linking consciousness which arises here as mixed with form, apart from the formless existence, arises in the form existences without sex, that is, without the sex denoted by the female or male faculty. In the sense-sphere existence, apart from the rebirth-linking of a congenital eunuch, it arises together with sex; thus it is twofold: with sex and without sex.

Sabhāvaṃ [M 2.0185] tattha ca dvidhāti tatthāpi ca yaṃ sa-bhāvaṃ, taṃ itthipurisabhāvānaṃ aññatarena saha uppattito duvidhameva hoti.

As to 'And therein that with sex is also twofold': even there, that which is with sex is indeed twofold due to its arising together with either the female or male sex.

Dve vā tayo vā dasakā omato ādinā sahāti yaṃ hetamettha “missaṃ amissa”nti duke ādibhūtaṃ rūpamissaṃ paṭisandhiviññāṇaṃ, tena saha vatthukāyadasakavasena dve vā, vatthukāyabhāvadasakavasena tayo vā dasakā omato uppajjanti, natthi ito paraṃ rūpaparihānīti. Taṃ panetaṃ evaṃ omakaparimāṇaṃ uppajjamānaṃ aṇḍajajalābujanāmikāsu dvīsu yonīsu jātiuṇṇāya ekena aṃsunā uddhaṭasappimaṇḍappamāṇaṃ kalalanti laddhasaṅkhaṃ hutvā uppajjati. Tattha yonīnaṃ gativasena sambhavabhedo veditabbo.

Two or three decads, at the minimum, along with the initial (consciousness): Herein, in the pair 'mixed and unmixed', that which is the initial rebirth-linking consciousness mixed with materiality—along with it, two decads arise by way of the base-decad and body-decad, or three decads by way of the base-decad, body-decad, and sex-decad, at the minimum. There is no further decrease in materiality beyond this. Furthermore, this aggregate of materiality, arising with such a minimal measure, in the two modes of birth known as egg-born and womb-born, arises having received the designation 'kalala', with the measure of a drop of clarified butter lifted out by a single fiber of fine wool. Therein, the distinction of origin should be understood by way of the destination of the modes of birth.

630. Etāsu hi,

630. For among these,

Niraye bhummavajjesu, devesu ca na yoniyo;

Tisso purimikā honti, catassopi gatittaye.

In hell and among the devas, excluding the earth-bound devas, the first three modes of birth do not exist; in the triad of destinations, all four exist.

Tattha [V 2.0183] devesu cāti casaddena yathā niraye ca bhummavajjesu ca devesu, evaṃ nijjhāmataṇhikapetesu ca purimikā tisso yoniyo na santīti veditabbā. Opapātikā eva hi te honti. Sese pana tiracchānapettivisayamanussasaṅkhāte gatittaye pubbe vajjitabhummadevesu ca catassopi yoniyo honti. Tattha,

Therein, by the word 'ca' in 'devesu ca', it should be understood that just as in hell and among the devas excluding the earth-bound ones, so too among the Nijjhāmataṇhika petas, the first three modes of birth do not exist. For they are indeed of spontaneous birth. However, in the remaining triad of destinations—designated as the animal, peta, and human realms—and among the earth-bound devas previously excluded, all four modes of birth exist. Therein,

Tiṃsa nava ceva rūpīsu, sattati ukkaṃsatotha rūpāni;

Saṃsedupapātayonisu, atha vā avakaṃsato tiṃsa.

Thirty and nine material phenomena in the form-beings; and seventy material phenomena at the maximum in moisture-born and spontaneous modes of birth; or, alternatively, thirty at the minimum.

Rūpībrahmesu tāva opapātikayonikesu cakkhusotavatthudasakānaṃ jīvitanavakassa cāti catunnaṃ kalāpānaṃ vasena tiṃsa ca nava ca paṭisandhiviññāṇena saha rūpāni uppajjanti. Rūpī brahme pana ṭhapetvā aññesu saṃsedajaopapātikayonikesu ukkaṃsato cakkhusotaghānajivhākāyavatthubhāvadasakānaṃ vasena sattati, tāni ca niccaṃ devesu. Tattha vaṇṇo gandho raso ojā catasso cāpi dhātuyo cakkhupasādo jīvitanti ayaṃ dasarūpaparimāṇo rūpapuñjo cakkhudasako nāma. Evaṃ sesā veditabbā[M 2.0186]. Avakaṃsato pana jaccandhabadhiraaghānakanapuṃsakassa jivhākāyavatthudasakānaṃ vasena tiṃsa rūpāni uppajjanti. Ukkaṃsāvakaṃsānaṃ pana antare anurūpato vikappo veditabbo.

First, among the form-realm brahmās of spontaneous birth, thirty and nine material phenomena arise along with the rebirth-linking consciousness by way of four groups: the eye-decad, ear-decad, base-decad, and the life-nonad. However, setting aside the form-realm brahmās, among other beings of moisture-born and spontaneous birth, seventy material phenomena arise at the maximum, by way of the eye-, ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, base-, and sex-decads; and these are always present among the devas. Therein, this group of material phenomena with a measure of ten—namely, color, odor, taste, nutritive essence, the four great elements, eye-sensitivity, and life-faculty—is called the eye-decad. The remaining groups should be understood in the same way. At the minimum, however, for one who is blind, deaf, anosmic, and sexually indeterminate from birth, thirty material phenomena arise by way of the tongue-, body-, and base-decads. Furthermore, between the maximum and minimum, the variation should be understood accordingly.

631. Evaṃ viditvā puna,

631. Having understood thus, again,

Khandhārammaṇagatihetu-vedanāpītivitakkavicārehi;

Bhedābhedaviseso, cutisandhīnaṃ pariññeyyo.

By means of aggregates, object, destination, cause, feeling, zest, initial application, and sustained application, the specific distinction of difference and non-difference between death and rebirth-linking should be fully understood.

Yā hesā missāmissato duvidhā paṭisandhi, yā cassā atītānantarā cuti, tāsaṃ imehi khandhādīhi bhedābhedaviseso ñātabboti attho.

The meaning is this: the specific distinction of difference and non-difference between this twofold rebirth-linking—which is mixed and unmixed—and its immediately preceding past death should be known by means of these aggregates and so forth.

Kathaṃ? Kadāci hi catukkhandhāya āruppacutiyā anantarā catukkhandhāva ārammaṇatopi abhinnā paṭisandhi hoti. Kadāci amahaggatabahiddhārammaṇāya mahaggataajjhattārammaṇā. Ayaṃ tāva arūpabhūmīsuyeva nayo. Kadāci pana catukkhandhāya arūpacutiyā anantarā pañcakkhandhā kāmāvacarapaṭisandhi[V 2.0184]. Kadāci pañcakkhandhāya kāmāvacaracutiyā rūpāvacaracutiyā vā anantarā catukkhandhā arūpapaṭisandhi. Evaṃ atītārammaṇāya cutiyā paccuppannārammaṇā paṭisandhi. Ekaccasugaticutiyā ekaccaduggatipaṭisandhi. Ahetukacutiyā sahetukapaṭisandhi. Duhetukacutiyā tihetukapaṭisandhi. Upekkhāsahagatacutiyā somanassasahagatapaṭisandhi. Appītikacutiyā sappītikapaṭisandhi. Avitakkacutiyā savitakkapaṭisandhi. Avicāracutiyā savicārapaṭisandhi. Avitakkāvicāracutiyā savitakkasavicārapaṭisandhīti tassa tassa viparītato ca yathāyogaṃ yojetabbaṃ.

How? Sometimes, immediately after a death with four aggregates in the formless realm, there is a rebirth-linking with four aggregates, undifferentiated also in respect to its object. Sometimes, after a death with a non-exalted, external object, there is a rebirth-linking with an exalted, internal object. This, for now, is the method only in the formless planes. Sometimes, however, immediately after a death with four aggregates in the formless realm, there is a sense-sphere rebirth-linking with five aggregates. Sometimes, immediately after a death with five aggregates in the sense-sphere or form-sphere, there is a formless rebirth-linking with four aggregates. Likewise, after a death with a past object, there is a rebirth-linking with a present object. After a death in a certain happy destination, there is a rebirth-linking in a certain unhappy destination. After a rootless death, there is a rebirth-linking with roots. After a two-rooted death, there is a three-rooted rebirth-linking. After a death accompanied by equanimity, there is a rebirth-linking accompanied by joy. After a death without zest, there is a rebirth-linking with zest. After a death without initial application, there is a rebirth-linking with initial application. After a death without sustained application, there is a rebirth-linking with sustained application. After a death without initial and sustained application, there is a rebirth-linking with initial and sustained application. Thus, for each of these cases, the connection should be made conversely as is appropriate.

632.

632.

Laddhapaccayamiti dhammamattametaṃ bhavantaramupeti;

Nāssa tato saṅkanti, na tato hetuṃ vinā hoti.

Having obtained its conditions, this mere phenomenon proceeds to another existence. There is no transition of it from there, nor does it arise from there without a cause.

Iti hetaṃ laddhapaccayaṃ rūpārūpadhammamattaṃ uppajjamānaṃ bhavantaramupetīti vuccati, na satto, na jīvo. Tassa ca nāpi atītabhavato idha saṅkanti atthi. Nāpi tato hetuṃ vinā idha pātubhāvo. Tayidaṃ pākaṭena manussacutipaṭisandhikkamena pakāsayissāma.

Thus, it is said that this, having obtained its conditions, arising as a mere phenomenon of materiality and immateriality, proceeds to another existence—not a being, not a soul. And there is no transition of it from a past existence to here, nor is there a manifestation here without a cause from there. This we shall explain by the evident process of human death and rebirth-linking.

Atītabhavasmiṃ [M 2.0187] hi sarasena upakkamena vā samāsannamaraṇassa asayhānaṃ sabbaṅgapaccaṅgasandhibandhanacchedakānaṃ māraṇantikavedanāsatthānaṃ sannipātaṃ asahantassa ātape pakkhittaharitatālapaṇṇamiva kamena upasussamāne sarīre niruddhesu cakkhādīsu indriyesu hadayavatthumatte patiṭṭhitesu kāyindriyamanindriyajīvitindriyesu taṅkhaṇāvasesahadayavatthusannissitaṃ viññāṇaṃ garukasamāsevitāsannapubbakatānaṃ aññataraṃ laddhāvasesapaccayasaṅkhārasaṅkhātaṃ kammaṃ, tadupaṭṭhāpitaṃ vā kammanimittagatinimittasaṅkhātaṃ visayaṃ ārabbha pavattati. Tadevaṃ pavattamānaṃ taṇhāvijjānaṃ appahīnattā avijjāpaṭicchāditādīnave tasmiṃ visaye taṇhā nāmeti, sahajātasaṅkhārā khipanti. Taṃ santativasena taṇhāya nāmiyamānaṃ saṅkhārehi khippamānaṃ orimatīrarukkhavinibaddharajjumālambitvā mātikātikkamako viya purimañca nissayaṃ jahati, aparañca kammasamuṭṭhāpitaṃ nissayaṃ assādayamānaṃ vā anassādayamānaṃ vā ārammaṇādīhiyeva paccayehi pavattatīti.

Indeed, in a past existence, for one whose death is near either through natural expiration or by external means, who cannot endure the onslaught of unbearable, sword-like death-pangs that sever the connections of all major and minor limbs; while the body, like a green palm-leaf cast in the sun, gradually withers; while the sense faculties such as the eye have ceased; and while the body, mind, and life faculties are established in the heart-base alone—at that moment, the consciousness, dependent on the remaining heart-base, proceeds by taking as its object either one of the following: kamma, designated as formations, which has obtained its remaining conditions, from among weighty, habitual, proximate, or previously performed kamma; or an object, designated as a kamma-sign or destination-sign, presented by that kamma. As it is thus proceeding, because craving and ignorance have not been abandoned, craving inclines it towards that object whose dangers are concealed by ignorance, and the co-nascent formations propel it. That consciousness, being inclined by craving and propelled by formations in the continuity of consciousness, is like a man who crosses a canal by holding onto a rope tied to a tree on the near bank; it abandons its former physical basis and proceeds, supported only by conditions such as its object, while either experiencing or not experiencing a new physical basis produced by kamma.

Ettha ca purimaṃ cavanato cuti. Pacchimaṃ bhavantarādipaṭisandhānato paṭisandhīti vuccati[V 2.0185]. Tadetaṃ nāpi purimabhavā idhāgataṃ, nāpi tato kammasaṅkhāranativisayādihetuṃ vinā pātubhūtanti veditabbaṃ.

Herein, the former consciousness is called 'cuti' (decease) because of its departure from an existence. The latter is called 'paṭisandhi' (rebirth-linking) because it links to the beginning of another existence. It should be understood that this consciousness has neither come here from a previous existence, nor has it arisen without a cause from that previous existence, such as kamma, formations, inclination, and object.

633.

633.

Siyuṃ nidassanānettha, paṭighosādikā atha;

Santānabandhato natthi, ekatā nāpi nānatā.

Herein, examples such as the echo may be cited. Furthermore, owing to the binding of the continuum, there is neither identity nor difference.

Ettha cetassa viññāṇassa purimabhavato idha anāgamane, atītabhavapariyāpannahetūti ca uppāde paṭighosa-padīpa-muddā-paṭibimbappakārā dhammā nidassanāni siyuṃ. Yathā hi paṭighosa-padīpa-muddā-chāyā saddādihetukā honti aññatra agantvā evamevaṃ idaṃ cittaṃ.

Herein, regarding the non-coming of this consciousness from a previous existence to this one, and its arising due to causes pertaining to a past existence, phenomena such as echoes, lamp flames, seal impressions, and reflections may serve as illustrations. For just as echoes, lamp flames, seal impressions, and shadows have sound and so forth as their causes and arise without having come from elsewhere, so too is this consciousness.

Ettha ca santānabandhato natthi ekatā nāpi nānatā. Yadi hi santānabandhe sati ekantamekatā bhaveyya, na khīrato dadhi sambhūtaṃ siyā. Athāpi ekantanānatā bhaveyya, na khīrassādhīno dadhi siyā. Esa nayo sabbahetuhetusamuppannesu. Evañca sati sabbalokavohāralopo [M 2.0188] siyā, so ca aniṭṭho. Tasmā ettha na ekantamekatā vā nānatā vā upagantabbāti.

Herein, owing to the binding of the continuum, there is neither absolute identity nor absolute difference. For if there were absolute identity in the continuum, curd would not arise from milk. And if there were absolute difference, curd would not be dependent on milk. This is the principle for all things arisen from their respective causes. And were this so, all worldly convention would be destroyed, which is undesirable. Therefore, herein neither absolute identity nor absolute difference should be adopted.

634. Etthāha – nanu evaṃ asaṅkantipātubhāve sati ye imasmiṃ manussattabhāve khandhā, tesaṃ niruddhattā, phalapaccayassa ca kammassa tattha agamanato aññassa aññato ca taṃ phalaṃ siyā, upabhuñjake ca asati kassa taṃ phalaṃ siyā, tasmā na sundaramidaṃ vidhānanti. Tatridaṃ vuccati –

634. Herein, one objects: 'Surely, if there is an arising without transference, then since the aggregates in this human existence have ceased, and since the kamma that is the condition for the fruit does not go there, would not that fruit belong to another and arise from another cause? And, there being no experiencer, whose fruit would it be? Therefore, this explanation is not sound.' To this, the reply is:

Santāne yaṃ phalaṃ etaṃ, nāññassa na ca aññato;

Bījānaṃ abhisaṅkhāro, etassatthassa sādhako.

That fruit which is in the continuum is not of another, nor is it from another; the conditioning of seeds is what establishes this meaning.

Ekasantānasmiṃ hi phalaṃ uppajjamānaṃ tattha ekantaekattanānattānaṃ paṭisiddhattā aññassāti vā aññatoti vā na hoti. Etassa ca panatthassa bījānaṃ abhisaṅkhāro sādhako. Ambabījādīnaṃ hi abhisaṅkhāresu katesu tassa bījassa santāne laddhapaccayo kālantare phalaviseso uppajjamāno na aññabījānaṃ, nāpi aññābhisaṅkhārapaccayā uppajjati[V 2.0186], na ca tāni bījāni, te abhisaṅkhārā vā phalaṭṭhānaṃ pāpuṇanti, evaṃ sampadamidaṃ veditabbaṃ. Vijjāsipposadhādīhi cāpi bālasarīre upayuttehi kālantare vuḍḍhasarīrādīsu phaladehi ayamattho veditabbo.

For when a fruit arises in a single continuum, it is not said to be 'of another' or 'from another,' because absolute identity and difference are rejected therein. The conditioning of seeds serves to establish this meaning. For when mango seeds and so on are conditioned, a particular fruit, having obtained its conditions, arises at a later time in the continuum of that seed; it is not the fruit of other seeds, nor does it arise from the conditioning of others as its cause. And neither those seeds nor that conditioning reaches the place where the fruit appears. The accomplishment of this principle should be understood in this way. This meaning should also be understood through knowledge, crafts, medicines, and so on, which, when applied to the body of a child, produce their fruit in the body of an adult at a later time.

Yampi vuttaṃ “upabhuñjake ca asati kassa taṃ phalaṃ siyā”ti, tattha,

And as to what was said: 'And, there being no experiencer, whose fruit would it be?'—to this, the reply is:

Phalassuppattiyā eva, siddhā bhuñjakasammuti;

Phaluppādena rukkhassa, yathā phalati sammuti.

The convention of an 'experiencer' is established simply by the arising of the fruit, just as the convention that a tree 'bears fruit' is established by the arising of fruit.

Yathā hi rukkhasaṅkhātānaṃ dhammānaṃ ekadesabhūtassa rukkhaphalassa uppattiyā eva rukkho phalatīti vā phalitoti vā vuccati, tathā devamanussasaṅkhātānaṃ khandhānaṃ ekadesabhūtassa upabhogasaṅkhātassa sukhadukkhaphalassa uppādeneva devo, manusso vā upabhuñjatīti vā, sukhito, dukkhitoti vā vuccati. Tasmā na ettha aññena upabhuñjakena nāma koci attho atthīti.

For just as, with the mere arising of a tree's fruit, which is a part of the phenomena designated as 'tree,' the tree is said 'to bear fruit' or 'to have fruited,' so too, with the mere arising of the fruit of pleasure and pain, which is designated as 'experience' and is a part of the aggregates designated as 'deva' or 'human,' a deva or a human is said 'to experience,' or 'to be happy' or 'unhappy.' Therefore, herein there is no need for any other thing called an 'experiencer.'

635. Yopi [M 2.0189] vadeyya “evaṃ santepi ete saṅkhārā vijjamānā vā phalassa paccayā siyuṃ, avijjamānā vā, yadi ca vijjamānā pavattikkhaṇeyeva nesaṃ vipākena bhavitabbaṃ, atha avijjamānā pavattito pubbe pacchā ca niccaṃ phalāvahā siyu”nti, so evaṃ vattabbo –

635. And should someone say: 'Even so, could these formations be conditions for the fruit whether they are existing or non-existing? If they are existing, their result ought to occur at the very moment of their occurrence. If they are non-existing, they would have to be perpetually fruit-bearing both before and after their occurrence,' they should be answered thus:

Katattā paccayā ete, na ca niccaṃ phalāvahā;

Pāṭibhogādikaṃ tattha, veditabbaṃ nidassanaṃ.

Because they have been performed, they are conditions, but they are not perpetually fruit-bearing. Herein, the example of a surety and so on should be understood.

Katattāyeva hi saṅkhārā attano phalassa paccayā honti, na vijjamānattā, avijjamānattā vā. Yathāha – “kāmāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākaṃ cakkhuviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hotī”tiādi (dha. sa. 431). Yathārahassa ca attano phalassa paccayā hutvā na puna phalāvahā honti vipākattā. Etassa catthassa vibhāvane idaṃ pāṭibhogādikaṃ nidassanaṃ veditabbaṃ. Yathā hi loke yo kassaci atthassa niyyātanatthaṃ pāṭibhogo hoti, bhaṇḍaṃ vā kiṇāti, iṇaṃ vā gaṇhāti, tassa taṃ kiriyākaraṇamattameva tadatthaniyyātanādimhi [V 2.0187] paccayo hoti, na kiriyāya vijjamānattaṃ, avijjamānattaṃ vā, na ca tadatthaniyyātanādito parampi dhārakova hoti. Kasmā? Niyyātanādīnaṃ katattā. Evaṃ katattāva saṅkhārāpi attano phalassa paccayā honti, na ca yathārahaṃ phaladānato parampi phalāvahā hontīti. Ettāvatā missāmissavasena dvedhāpi vattamānassa paṭisandhiviññāṇassa saṅkhārapaccayā pavatti dīpitā hoti.

For formations are conditions for their own fruit simply because they have been performed, not because of their existence or non-existence. As it is said: 'Due to the performance and accumulation of wholesome kamma of the sense-sphere, resultant eye-consciousness arises,' and so on. And having become conditions for their own respective fruits, they are not fruit-bearing again, because the result has been given. To clarify this meaning, this example of a surety and so on should be understood. For in the world, when someone acts as a surety for the settlement of some matter, or buys goods, or takes a loan, the mere performance of that action is the condition for the settlement of that matter, not the existence or non-existence of the action. Nor does one remain liable after the matter has been settled. Why? Because the settlement has been performed. In the same way, formations are conditions for their own fruit simply because they have been performed, and after giving their fruit appropriately, they are no longer fruit-bearing. Thus far, the process of rebirth-linking consciousness, which occurs in two ways, mixed and unmixed, has been shown as conditioned by formations.

636. Idāni sabbesveva tesu bāttiṃsavipākaviññāṇesu sammohavighātatthaṃ,

636. Now, to dispel confusion regarding all those thirty-two resultant consciousnesses:

Paṭisandhipavattīnaṃ, vasenete bhavādisu;

Vijānitabbā saṅkhārā, yathā yesañca paccayā.

These formations should be understood by way of rebirth-linking and the life-continuum in the various existences and so on: for which consciousnesses they are conditions, and in what way.

Tattha tayo bhavā, catasso yoniyo, pañca gatiyo, satta viññāṇaṭṭhitiyo, nava sattāvāsāti ete bhavādayo nāma. Etesu bhavādīsu paṭisandhiyaṃ pavatte ca ete yesaṃ vipākaviññāṇānaṃ paccayā, yathā ca paccayā honti, tathā vijānitabbāti attho.

Herein, the three existences, four modes of generation, five destinations, seven stations of consciousness, and nine abodes of beings—these are what are called 'existences and so on.' The meaning is that it should be understood for which resultant consciousnesses these formations are conditions, both in rebirth-linking and in the course of life within these existences, and in what way they are conditions.

Tattha [M 2.0190] puññābhisaṅkhāre tāva kāmāvacaraaṭṭhacetanābhedo puññābhisaṅkhāro avisesena kāmabhave sugatiyaṃ navannaṃ vipākaviññāṇānaṃ paṭisandhiyaṃ nānakkhaṇikakammapaccayena ceva upanissayapaccayena cāti dvedhā paccayo. Rūpāvacarapañcakusalacetanābhedo puññābhisaṅkhāro rūpabhave paṭisandhiyaṃ eva pañcannaṃ.

Among these, with regard to meritorious formations, firstly, the meritorious formation comprising the eight kinds of sense-sphere wholesome volitions is, in general, a twofold condition for the nine resultant consciousnesses at rebirth-linking in a happy destination within the sense-sphere existence, namely, by way of different-moment kamma condition and by way of decisive support condition. The meritorious formation comprising the five kinds of form-sphere wholesome volitions is a condition for the five resultant consciousnesses only at rebirth-linking in the form-sphere existence.

Vuttappabhedakāmāvacaro pana kāmabhave sugatiyaṃ upekkhāsahagatāhetumanoviññāṇadhātuvajjānaṃ sattannaṃ parittavipākaviññāṇānaṃ vuttanayeneva dvedhā paccayo pavatte, no paṭisandhiyaṃ. Sveva rūpabhave pañcannaṃ vipākaviññāṇānaṃ tatheva paccayo pavatte, no paṭisandhiyaṃ. Kāmabhave pana duggatiyaṃ aṭṭhannampi parittavipākaviññāṇānaṃ tatheva paccayo pavatte, no paṭisandhiyaṃ. Tattha niraye mahāmoggallānattherassa narakacārikādīsu iṭṭhārammaṇasamāyoge so paccayo hoti, tiracchānesu pana petamahiddhikesu ca iṭṭhārammaṇaṃ labbhatiyeva.

Furthermore, the aforementioned sense-sphere meritorious formation, in a happy destination within the sense-sphere existence, is a twofold condition in the aforementioned manner for seven limited resultant consciousnesses—excluding the rootless mind-consciousness-element accompanied by equanimity—during the course of existence, but not at rebirth-linking. That same formation is likewise a condition for five resultant consciousnesses in the form-sphere existence during the course of existence, but not at rebirth-linking. Furthermore, in an unhappy destination within the sense-sphere existence, it is likewise a condition for all eight limited resultant consciousnesses during the course of existence, but not at rebirth-linking. Therein, in hell, during the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna’s tour of hell and so forth, that formation becomes a condition upon encountering an agreeable object. Moreover, among animals and powerful hungry ghosts, an agreeable object is indeed obtainable.

Sveva kāmabhave sugatiyaṃ soḷasannampi kusalavipākaviññāṇānaṃ tatheva paccayo pavatte ca [V 2.0188] paṭisandhiyañca. Avisesena pana puññābhisaṅkhāro rūpabhave dasannaṃ vipākaviññāṇānaṃ tatheva paccayo pavatte ca paṭisandhiyañca.

That same formation, in a happy destination within the sense-sphere existence, is likewise a condition for all sixteen wholesome resultant consciousnesses both during the course of existence and at rebirth-linking. Furthermore, the meritorious formation in general is likewise a condition for the ten resultant consciousnesses in the form-sphere existence both during the course of existence and at rebirth-linking.

Dvādasākusalacetanābhedo apuññābhisaṅkhāro kāmabhave duggatiyaṃ ekassa viññāṇassa tatheva paccayo paṭisandhiyaṃ, no pavatte. Channaṃ pavatte, no paṭisandhiyaṃ. Sattannampi akusalavipākaviññāṇānaṃ pavatte ca paṭisandhiyañca.

The demeritorious formation comprising the twelve unwholesome volitions, in an unhappy destination within the sense-sphere existence, is likewise a condition for one consciousness at rebirth-linking, but not during the course of existence. For the other six, it is a condition during the course of existence, but not at rebirth-linking. In general, however, it is a condition for all seven unwholesome resultant consciousnesses both during the course of existence and at rebirth-linking.

Kāmabhave pana sugatiyaṃ tesaṃyeva sattannaṃ tatheva paccayo pavatte, no paṭisandhiyaṃ. Rūpabhave catunnaṃ vipākaviññāṇānaṃ tatheva paccayo pavatte, no paṭisandhiyaṃ. So ca kho kāmāvacare aniṭṭharūpadassanasaddasavanavasena, brahmaloke pana aniṭṭharūpādayo nāma natthi. Tathā kāmāvacaradevalokepi.

Furthermore, in a happy destination within the sense-sphere existence, it is likewise a condition for those same seven consciousnesses only during the course of existence, not at rebirth-linking. In the form-sphere existence, it is likewise a condition for four resultant consciousnesses during the course of existence, not at rebirth-linking. And that demeritorious formation is indeed a condition in the sense-sphere by way of seeing disagreeable forms and hearing disagreeable sounds. In the Brahma-world, however, there are no such things as disagreeable forms and so on. Likewise in the sense-sphere celestial worlds.

Āneñjābhisaṅkhāro arūpabhave catunnaṃ vipākaviññāṇānaṃ tatheva paccayo pavatte ca paṭisandhiyañca.

The imperturbable formation is likewise a condition for the four resultant consciousnesses in the formless existence, both during the course of existence and at rebirth-linking.

Evaṃ [M 2.0191] tāva bhavesu paṭisandhipavattīnaṃ vasena ete saṅkhārā yesaṃ paccayā, yathā ca paccayā honti, tathā vijānitabbā. Eteneva nayena yoniādīsupi veditabbā.

Thus, firstly, it should be understood for which resultant consciousnesses these formations are conditions in the various existences by way of rebirth-linking and the course of existence, and in what manner they are conditions. By this same method, they should also be understood in regard to the modes of birth and so on.

637. Tatridaṃ ādito paṭṭhāya mukhamattapakāsanaṃ – imesu hi saṅkhāresu yasmā puññābhisaṅkhāro tāva dvīsu bhavesu paṭisandhiṃ datvā sabbamattano vipākaṃ janeti. Tathā aṇḍajādīsu catūsu yonīsu, devamanussasaṅkhātāsu dvīsu gatīsu, nānattakāyanānattasaññīnānattakāyaekattasaññī-ekattakāyanānattasaññī-ekattakāyaekattasaññīsaṅkhātāsu catūsu viññāṇaṭṭhitīsu. Asaññasattāvāse panesa rūpamattamevābhisaṅkharotīti catūsuyeva sattāvāsesu ca paṭisandhiṃ datvā sabbamattano vipākaṃ janeti. Tasmā esa etesu dvīsu bhavesu, catūsu yonīsu, dvīsu gatīsu, catūsu viññāṇaṭṭhitīsu, catūsu sattāvāsesu ca ekavīsatiyā vipākaviññāṇānaṃ vuttanayeneva paccayo hoti yathāsambhavaṃ paṭisandhiyaṃ pavatte ca.

637. Herein, this is but a brief exposition from the beginning: For, among these formations, since the meritorious formation, firstly, having given rebirth in two existences, generates its entire result; similarly in the four modes of birth, such as egg-born; in the two destinations, designated as devas and humans; and in the four stations of consciousness, designated as beings with diverse bodies and diverse perceptions, beings with diverse bodies and uniform perception, beings with uniform bodies and diverse perceptions, and beings with uniform bodies and uniform perception. Furthermore, since in the abode of non-percipient beings this formation conditions only matter, it is thus that, having given rebirth in just four abodes of beings, it generates its entire result. Therefore, this formation is a condition for the twenty-one resultant consciousnesses in these two existences, four modes of birth, two destinations, four stations of consciousness, and four abodes of beings, in the aforementioned manner, as is applicable, both at rebirth-linking and during the course of existence.

Apuññābhisaṅkhāro pana yasmā ekasmiṃyeva kāmabhave catūsu yonīsu, avasesāsu tīsu gatīsu[V 2.0189], nānattakāyaekattasaññīsaṅkhātāya ekissā viññāṇaṭṭhitiyā, tādiseyeva ca ekasmiṃ sattāvāse paṭisandhivasena vipaccati, tasmā esa ekasmiṃ bhave, catūsu yonīsu, tīsu gatīsu, ekissā viññāṇaṭṭhitiyā, ekamhi ca sattāvāse sattannaṃ vipākaviññāṇānaṃ vuttanayeneva paccayo paṭisandhiyaṃ pavatte ca.

Furthermore, since the demeritorious formation ripens by way of rebirth-linking in only one existence—the sense-sphere existence—in the four modes of birth, in the remaining three destinations, in the one station of consciousness designated as 'beings with diverse bodies and uniform perception,' and in one such corresponding abode of beings; therefore, this formation is a condition for the seven resultant consciousnesses in that one existence, four modes of birth, three destinations, one station of consciousness, and one abode of beings, in the aforementioned manner, both at rebirth-linking and during the course of existence.

Āneñjābhisaṅkhāro pana yasmā ekasmiṃyeva arūpabhave, ekissā opapātikayoniyā, ekissā devagatiyā, ākāsānañcāyatanādikāsu tīsu viññāṇaṭṭhitīsu, ākāsānañcāyatanādikesu ca catūsu sattāvāsesu paṭisandhivasena vipaccati, tasmā esa ekasmiṃ bhave, ekissā yoniyā, ekissā gatiyā, tīsu viññāṇaṭṭhitīsu, catūsu sattāvāsesu catunnaṃ viññāṇānaṃ vuttanayeneva paccayo hoti paṭisandhiyaṃ pavatte cāti. Evaṃ,

Furthermore, since the imperturbable formation ripens by way of rebirth-linking in only one existence—the formless existence—in one mode of birth, that of spontaneous arising, in one destination, that of devas, in the three stations of consciousness beginning with the base of infinite space, and in the four abodes of beings beginning with the base of infinite space; therefore, this formation is a condition for the four consciousnesses in that one existence, one mode of birth, one destination, three stations of consciousness, and four abodes of beings, in the aforementioned manner, both at rebirth-linking and during the course of existence. Thus,

Paṭisandhipavattīnaṃ[M 2.0192], vasenete bhavādisu;

Vijānitabbā saṅkhārā, yathā yesañca paccayāti.

By way of rebirth-linking and life's course, in existences and so on, these formations should be understood: how, and for which consciousnesses, they are a condition.

Ayaṃ “saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇa”nti padasmiṃ vitthārakathā.

This is the detailed exposition on the phrase, 'Conditioned by formations, consciousness arises.'

Viññāṇapaccayānāmarūpapadavitthārakathā

The Detailed Exposition on the Phrase 'Conditioned by Consciousness, Name-and-Form'

638. Viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpapade –

638. In the phrase 'Conditioned by consciousness, name-and-form':

Vibhāgā nāmarūpānaṃ, bhavādīsu pavattito;

Saṅgahā paccayanayā, viññātabbo vinicchayo.

The determination should be known through: the analysis of name-and-form, its occurrence in existences and so on, its summary, and the method of conditionality.

Vibhāgā nāmarūpānanti ettha hi nāmanti ārammaṇābhimukhaṃ namanato vedanādayo tayo khandhā, rūpanti cattāri mahābhūtāni catunnañca mahābhūtānaṃ upādāyarūpaṃ. Tesaṃ vibhāgo khandhaniddese vuttoyevāti. Evaṃ tāvettha vibhāgā nāmarūpānaṃ viññātabbo vinicchayo.

Herein, regarding 'the analysis of name-and-form': 'name' refers to the three aggregates beginning with feeling, so called because of their 'bending' (namana) towards an object. 'Form' refers to the four great elements and the material form derived from and dependent on the four great elements. The analysis of these has already been stated in the Exposition of the Aggregates. Thus, firstly, the determination should be known here through the analysis of name-and-form.

Bhavādīsu pavattitoti ettha ca nāmaṃ ekaṃ sattāvāsaṃ ṭhapetvā sabbabhavayonigativiññāṇaṭṭhitisesasattāvāsesu [V 2.0190] pavattati, rūpaṃ dvīsu bhavesu, catūsu yonīsu, pañcasu gatīsu, purimāsu catūsu viññāṇaṭṭhitīsu, pañcasu sattāvāsesu pavattati.

And here, concerning 'its occurrence in existences and so forth,' name, excepting one abode of beings, occurs in all existences, modes of birth, destinies, stations of consciousness, and the remaining abodes of beings. Form occurs in two existences, four modes of birth, five destinies, the first four stations of consciousness, and five abodes of beings.

Evaṃ pavattamāne ca etasmiṃ nāmarūpe yasmā abhāvakagabbhaseyyakānaṃ aṇḍajānañca paṭisandhikkhaṇe vatthukāyadasakavasena rūpato dvesantatisīsāni, tayo ca arūpino khandhā pātubhavanti, tasmā tesaṃ vitthārena rūparūpato vīsati dhammā, tayo ca arūpino khandhāti ete tevīsati dhammā viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpanti veditabbā. Aggahitaggahaṇena pana ekasantatisīsato nava rūpadhamme apanetvā cuddasa. Sabhāvakānaṃ bhāvadasakaṃ pakkhipitvā tettiṃsa, tesampi aggahitaggahaṇena santatisīsadvayato aṭṭhārasa rūpadhamme apanetvā pannarasa.

And while this name-and-form is thus occurring, since at the moment of rebirth-linking for those womb-born beings who are without the gender faculty and for the egg-born, two continuity-heads of form appear by way of the base-decade and the body-decade, and three immaterial aggregates appear, therefore, for them, in detail, twenty phenomena from concrete form and three immaterial aggregates—these twenty-three phenomena—are to be understood as 'name-and-form conditioned by consciousness.' However, by the method of taking only what has not yet been taken, removing nine material phenomena from one continuity-head, fourteen remain. For those with the gender faculty, including the gender-decade, there are thirty-three; and for them too, by the method of taking only what has not yet been taken, removing eighteen material phenomena from two continuity-heads, fifteen remain.

Yasmā ca opapātikasattesu brahmakāyikādīnaṃ paṭisandhikkhaṇe cakkhusotavatthudasakānaṃ, jīvitindriyanavakassa ca vasena rūpato cattāri santatisīsāni, tayo ca arūpino khandhā pātubhavanti, tasmā tesaṃ vitthārena rūparūpato ekūnacattālīsa dhammā, tayo ca arūpino khandhāti [M 2.0193] ete bācattālīsa dhammā viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpanti veditabbā. Aggahitaggahaṇena pana santatisīsattayato sattavīsati dhamme apanetvā pannarasa.

And since for spontaneously born beings such as the Brahmā-group deities, at the moment of rebirth-linking, four continuity-heads of form appear by way of the eye-decade, ear-decade, and base-decade, and the life-faculty nonad, and three immaterial aggregates appear, therefore, for them, in detail, thirty-nine phenomena from concrete form and three immaterial aggregates—these forty-two phenomena—are to be understood as 'name-and-form conditioned by consciousness.' However, by the method of taking only what has not yet been taken, removing twenty-seven phenomena from three continuity-heads, fifteen remain.

Kāmabhave pana yasmā sesaopapātikānaṃ, saṃsedajānaṃ vā sabhāvakaparipuṇṇāyatanānaṃ paṭisandhikkhaṇe rūpato satta santatisīsāni, tayo ca arūpino khandhā pātubhavanti, tasmā tesaṃ vitthārena rūparūpato sattati dhammā, tayo ca arūpino khandhāti ete tesattati dhammā viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpanti veditabbā. Aggahitaggahaṇena pana rūpasantatisīsachakkato catupaññāsa dhamme apanetvā ekūnavīsati. Esa ukkaṃso. Avakaṃsena pana taṃtaṃrūpasantatisīsavikalānaṃ tassa tassa vasena hāpetvā hāpetvā saṅkhepato vitthārato ca paṭisandhiyaṃ viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpasaṅkhā veditabbā.

In the sensual realm, however, since for the remaining spontaneously born beings, or for those born from moisture who possess the gender faculty and have complete sense bases, at the moment of rebirth-linking, seven continuity-heads of form and three immaterial aggregates appear, therefore, for them, in detail, seventy phenomena from concrete form and three immaterial aggregates—these seventy-three phenomena—are to be understood as 'name-and-form conditioned by consciousness.' However, by the method of taking only what has not yet been taken, removing fifty-four phenomena from the six continuity-heads of form, nineteen remain. This is the maximum. By the minimum, however, for those deficient in this or that continuity-head of form, by reducing accordingly for each deficiency, the reckoning of name-and-form conditioned by consciousness at rebirth-linking should be understood both in brief and in detail.

Arūpīnaṃ pana tayova arūpino khandhā. Asaññīnaṃ rūpato jīvitindriyanavakamevāti. Esa tāva paṭisandhiyaṃ nayo.

For formless beings, however, there are just the three immaterial aggregates. For non-percipient beings, there is just the life-faculty nonad from the material side. This, then, is the method regarding rebirth-linking.

Pavatte pana sabbattha rūpappavattidese paṭisandhicittassa ṭhitikkhaṇe paṭisandhicittena saha pavattaututo [V 2.0191] utusamuṭṭhānaṃ suddhaṭṭhakaṃ pātubhavati. Paṭisandhicittaṃ pana rūpaṃ na samuṭṭhāpeti. Tañhi yathā papāte patitapuriso parassa paccayo hotuṃ na sakkoti, evaṃ vatthudubbalatāya dubbalattā rūpaṃ samuṭṭhāpetuṃ na sakkoti. Paṭisandhicittato pana uddhaṃ paṭhamabhavaṅgato pabhuti cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ suddhaṭṭhakaṃ, saddapātubhāvakāle paṭisandhikkhaṇato uddhaṃ pavattaututo ceva cittato ca saddanavakaṃ, ye pana kabaḷīkārāhārūpajīvino gabbhaseyyakasattā, tesaṃ,

In the course of existence, however, wherever form occurs, at the static moment of the rebirth-linking consciousness, the temperature-originated pure octad appears, arising from the temperature that occurs together with the rebirth-linking consciousness. The rebirth-linking consciousness, however, does not produce form. For just as a man falling from a precipice cannot be a support for another, so too, because it is weak due to the weakness of its base, it cannot produce form. After the rebirth-linking consciousness, however, starting from the first life-continuum, the consciousness-originated pure octad arises. At the time of the manifestation of sound, after the moment of rebirth-linking, the sound-nonad arises from both the occurring temperature and from consciousness. As for those womb-born beings who subsist on edible food, for them,

“Yañcassa bhuñjati mātā, annaṃ pānañca bhojanaṃ;

Tena so tattha yāpeti, mātukucchigato naro”ti. –

“Whatever food his mother consumes, solid food, drink, and nourishment, by that he is sustained there, the man abiding in his mother’s womb.”

Vacanato mātarā ajjhoharitāhārena anugate sarīre, opapātikānaṃ sabbapaṭhamaṃ attano mukhagataṃ kheḷaṃ ajjhoharaṇakāle āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ suddhaṭṭhakanti idaṃ āhārasamuṭṭhānassa suddhaṭṭhakassa, utucittasamuṭṭhānānañca ukkaṃsato dvinnaṃ navakānaṃ vasena chabbīsatividhaṃ, pubbe ekekacittakkhaṇe [M 2.0194] tikkhattuṃ uppajjamānaṃ vuttaṃ kammasamuṭṭhānañca sattatividhanti channavutividhaṃ rūpaṃ, tayo ca arūpino khandhāti samāsato navanavuti dhammā. Yasmā vā saddo aniyato kadācideva pātubhāvato, tasmā duvidhampi taṃ apanetvā ime sattanavuti dhammā yathāsambhavaṃ sabbasattānaṃ viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpanti veditabbaṃ. Tesaṃ hi suttānampi pamattānampi khādantānampi pivantānampi divā ca rattiñca ete viññāṇapaccayā pavattanti. Tañca nesaṃ viññāṇapaccayabhāvaṃ parato vaṇṇayissāma.

Based on this statement, in the body pervaded by food swallowed by the mother, the nutriment-originated pure octad arises. For spontaneously born beings, it arises at the time of first swallowing the saliva in their mouth. Thus, by way of this nutriment-originated pure octad and, at maximum, the two nonads originated from temperature and consciousness, there is this twenty-six-fold form. And with the seventy-fold kamma-originated form, which was previously said to arise three times in each mind-moment, there are ninety-six kinds of form. Together with the three immaterial aggregates, there are, in brief, ninety-nine phenomena. Or, because sound is indeterminate, appearing only occasionally, therefore, removing that twofold sound, these ninety-seven phenomena should be understood as 'name-and-form conditioned by consciousness' for all beings, according to what is possible. For them, indeed, whether sleeping or heedless, eating or drinking, by day and by night, these phenomena proceed conditioned by consciousness. And we will explain this fact of their being conditioned by consciousness later on.

Yampanetamettha kammajarūpaṃ, taṃ bhavayonigatiṭhitisattāvāsesu sabbapaṭhamaṃ patiṭṭhahantampi tisamuṭṭhānikarūpena anupatthaddhaṃ na sakkoti saṇṭhātuṃ, nāpi tisamuṭṭhānikaṃ tena anupatthaddhaṃ. Atha kho vātabbhāhatāpi catuddisā vavatthāpitā naḷakalāpiyo viya, ūmivegabbhāhatāpi mahāsamudde katthaci laddhapatiṭṭhā bhinnavāhanikā viya ca aññamaññupatthaddhānevetāni apatamānāni saṇṭhahitvā ekampi vassaṃ dvepi vassāni…pe… vassasatampi yāva tesaṃ sattānaṃ āyukkhayo vā puññakkhayo vā, tāva pavattantīti. Evaṃ bhavādīsu pavattitopettha viññātabbo vinicchayo.

Whatever kamma-born form exists here, even though it is the very first to be established in the existences, modes of birth, destinies, stations of consciousness, and abodes of beings, it cannot endure if unsupported by form originated from the three other sources. Nor can the form from the three sources endure if unsupported by it. Rather, just as bundles of reeds, set up leaning against one another from four directions, stand firm even when buffeted by the wind, and just as broken-down watercraft in the great ocean, having found some footing, endure by clinging together even when struck by the force of the waves, so too these forms, by mutually supporting one another, stand without collapsing. They continue for one year, two years... even a hundred years, for as long as the lifespan or the merit of those beings is not exhausted. In this way, the determination concerning occurrence in existences and so forth should also be understood here.

639. Saṅgahāti ettha ca yaṃ āruppe pavattipaṭisandhīsu, pañcavokārabhave ca pavattiyaṃ viññāṇapaccayā [V 2.0192] nāmameva, yañca asaññesu sabbattha, pañcavokārabhave ca pavattiyaṃ viññāṇapaccayā rūpameva, yañca pañcavokārabhave sabbattha viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpaṃ, taṃ sabbaṃ nāmañca rūpañca nāmarūpañca nāmarūpanti evaṃ ekadesasarūpekasesanayena saṅgahetvā viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpanti veditabbaṃ.

639. Furthermore, here, with regard to 'by way of synthesis': whatever in the formless realm, during the course of life and at rebirth-linking, and in the five-constituent existence, during the course of life, is nāma only, conditioned by consciousness; and whatever in the non-percipient realms, everywhere, and in the five-constituent existence, during the course of life, is rūpa only, conditioned by consciousness; and whatever in the five-constituent existence, everywhere, is nāmarūpa, conditioned by consciousness—all of that, namely nāma, rūpa, and nāmarūpa, having been synthesized by the method of partial identity and single remainder as 'nāmarūpa', should be understood as 'nāmarūpa conditioned by consciousness'.

Asaññesu viññāṇābhāvā ayuttanti ce, nāyuttaṃ. Idampi,

If it is said that this is inappropriate due to the absence of consciousness in the non-percipient beings, it is not inappropriate. This too is stated:

Nāmarūpassa yaṃ hetu, viññāṇaṃ taṃ dvidhā mataṃ;

Vipākamavipākañca, yuttameva yato idaṃ.

The consciousness that is a cause for name-and-form is considered twofold: resultant and non-resultant; therefore, this is indeed appropriate.

Yañhi nāmarūpassa hetu viññāṇaṃ, taṃ vipākāvipākabhedato dvedhā mataṃ. Idañca asaññasattesu kammasamuṭṭhānattā pañcavokārabhave pavattaabhisaṅkhāraviññāṇapaccayā rūpaṃ. Tathā pañcavokāre pavattiyaṃ kusalādicittakkhaṇe kammasamuṭṭhānanti yuttameva idaṃ. Evaṃ saṅgahatopettha viññātabbo vinicchayo.

For the consciousness that is a cause for nāmarūpa is considered twofold, distinguished as resultant and non-resultant. And this rūpa in the non-percipient beings, being kamma-originated, is conditioned by the volitional consciousness that occurred in a five-constituent existence. Likewise, in the five-constituent existence, during the course of life, at the moment of a wholesome or other consciousness, the kamma-originated rūpa is conditioned by the volitional consciousness that occurred in a five-constituent existence. Therefore, this is indeed appropriate. In this way, the determination here should be understood also by way of synthesis.

640. Paccayanayāti [M 2.0195] ettha hi,

640. And here, concerning 'by way of the conditional method':

Nāmassa pākaviññāṇaṃ, navadhā hoti paccayo;

Vatthurūpassa navadhā, sesarūpassa aṭṭhadhā.

Resultant consciousness is a condition for name in nine ways; for the base-form, in nine ways; for the remaining form, in eight ways.

Abhisaṅkhāraviññāṇaṃ, hoti rūpassa ekadhā;

Tadaññaṃ pana viññāṇaṃ, tassa tassa yathārahaṃ.

Volitional consciousness is a condition for rūpa in one way; but other consciousness is a condition for each of these respectively, as is appropriate.

Yañhetaṃ paṭisandhiyaṃ pavattiyaṃ vā vipākasaṅkhātaṃ nāmaṃ, tassa rūpamissassa vā amissassa vā paṭisandhikaṃ vā aññaṃ vā vipākaviññāṇaṃ sahajātaaññamaññanissayasampayuttavipākāhārindriyaatthiavigatapaccayehi navadhā paccayo hoti.

Whatever nāma is designated as resultant, whether at rebirth-linking or during the course of life, for that nāma, whether mixed with rūpa or not mixed, the resultant consciousness—be it at rebirth-linking or otherwise—is a condition in nine ways: by way of conascence, mutuality, support, association, result, nutriment, faculty, presence, and non-disappearance conditions.

Vatthurūpassa paṭisandhiyaṃ sahajātaaññamaññanissayavipākāhārindriyavippayuttaatthiavigatapaccayehi [V 2.0193] navadhā paccayo hoti. Ṭhapetvā pana vatthurūpaṃ sesarūpassa imesu navasu aññamaññapaccayaṃ apanetvā sesehi aṭṭhahi paccayehi paccayo hoti.

For the base-form at rebirth-linking, it is a condition in nine ways: by way of conascence, mutuality, support, result, nutriment, faculty, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance conditions. However, excluding the base-form, for the remaining form, it is a condition by the remaining eight conditions, omitting the mutuality condition from these nine.

Abhisaṅkhāraviññāṇaṃ pana asaññasattarūpassa vā pañcavokārabhave vā kammajassa rūpassa suttantikapariyāyato upanissayavasena ekadhāva paccayo hoti. Avasesaṃ paṭhamabhavaṅgato pabhuti sabbampi viññāṇaṃ tassa tassa nāmarūpassa yathārahaṃ paccayo hotīti veditabbaṃ. Vitthārato pana tassa paccayanaye dassiyamāne sabbāpi paṭṭhānakathā vitthāretabbā hotīti na naṃ ārabhāma.

Volitional consciousness, however, is a condition in one way by way of decisive support according to the Suttanta exposition for the kamma-born form of either the non-percipient beings or in the five-constituent existence. The rest, from the first life-continuum onwards, all consciousness should be understood as a condition for that respective name-and-form as appropriate. But when the method of conditions is shown in detail, the entire Paṭṭhāna would have to be elaborated; therefore, we do not undertake that.

Tattha siyā – kathaṃ panetaṃ jānitabbaṃ “paṭisandhināmarūpaṃ viññāṇapaccayā hotī”ti? Suttato yuttito ca. Sutte hi “cittānuparivattino dhammā”tiādinā (dha. sa. dukamātikā 62) nayena bahudhā vedanādīnaṃ viññāṇapaccayatā siddhā. Yuttito pana,

Here, one might ask: But how is it to be understood that 'rebirth-linking name-and-form is conditioned by consciousness'? By the Suttas and by reasoning. For in the Suttas, in many ways, such as by the principle 'states that revolve around consciousness' (Dhs. Dukamātikā §62), the fact that feeling and the rest are conditioned by consciousness is established. But by reasoning:

Cittajena hi rūpena, idha diṭṭhena sijjhati;

Adiṭṭhassāpi rūpassa, viññāṇaṃ paccayo iti.

For here, through mind-originated form that is seen, it is established that consciousness is a condition even for form that is unseen.

Citte hi pasanne appasanne vā tadanurūpāni rūpāni uppajjamānāni diṭṭhāni. Diṭṭhena ca adiṭṭhassa anumānaṃ hotīti iminā idha diṭṭhena cittajarūpena adiṭṭhassāpi paṭisandhirūpassa viññāṇaṃ paccayo hotīti jānitabbametaṃ. Kammasamuṭṭhānassāpi [M 2.0196] hi tassa cittasamuṭṭhānasseva viññāṇapaccayatā paṭṭhāne āgatāti. Evaṃ paccayanayatopettha viññātabbo vinicchayoti.

For when the mind is serene or agitated, corresponding forms are seen arising. And from what is seen, the unseen can be inferred. Thus, by this mind-originated form that is seen here, it should be understood that consciousness is a condition even for the unseen rebirth-linking form. For the fact that even that kamma-originated form is conditioned by consciousness, just like mind-originated form, is stated in the Paṭṭhāna. Thus, the determination here should also be understood by way of the conditional method.

Ayaṃ “viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpa”nti padasmiṃ vitthārakathā.

This is the detailed explanation of the phrase 'conditioned by consciousness is name-and-form'.

Nāmarūpapaccayāsaḷāyatanapadavitthārakathā

The Detailed Explanation of the Phrase 'Conditioned by Name-and-Form is the Six Sense Bases'

641. Nāmarūpapaccayā saḷāyatanapade –

641. In the phrase 'conditioned by name-and-form is the six sense bases':

Nāmaṃ khandhattayaṃ rūpaṃ, bhūtavatthādikaṃ mataṃ;

Katekasesaṃ taṃ tassa, tādisasseva paccayo.

Nāma is the three aggregates; rūpa is considered the primary elements, the bases, and so forth. That nāmarūpa, treated by single remainder, is a condition for that saḷāyatana, which is treated in the same way.

Yañhetaṃ [V 2.0194] saḷāyatanasseva paccayabhūtaṃ nāmarūpaṃ, tattha nāmanti vedanādikkhandhattayaṃ, rūpaṃ pana sasantatipariyāpannaṃ niyamato cattāri bhūtāni cha vatthūni jīvitindriyanti evaṃ bhūtavatthādikaṃ matanti veditabbaṃ. Taṃ pana nāmañca rūpañca nāmarūpañca nāmarūpanti evaṃ katekasesaṃ chaṭṭhāyatanañca saḷāyatanañca saḷāyatananti evaṃ katekasesasseva saḷāyatanassa paccayoti veditabbaṃ. Kasmā? Yasmā āruppe nāmameva paccayo, tañca chaṭṭhāyatanasseva na aññassa. “Nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatana”nti (vibha. 322) hi vibhaṅge vuttaṃ.

Regarding that nāmarūpa which is a condition for the six sense bases: therein, 'nāma' should be understood as the three aggregates beginning with feeling; and 'rūpa' should be understood as the primary elements, bases, and so forth, namely the four primary elements, the six bases, and the life faculty, which are definitely included in one's own continuity. Furthermore, it should be understood that this nāmarūpa—which by the method of single remainder comprises nāma, rūpa, and nāmarūpa—is a condition for the six sense bases, which are themselves treated by the same method of single remainder, comprising the sixth sense base and the six sense bases. Why? Because in the formless realm, only nāma is a condition, and it is a condition only for the sixth sense base, not for any other. For it is said in the Vibhaṅga: 'Conditioned by nāma is the sixth sense base' (Vibh 322).

Tattha siyā – kathaṃ panetaṃ jānitabbaṃ “nāmarūpaṃ saḷāyatanassa paccayo”ti? Nāmarūpabhāve bhāvato. Tassa tassa hi nāmassa rūpassa ca bhāve taṃ taṃ āyatanaṃ hoti, na aññathā. Sā panassa tabbhāvabhāvitā paccayanayasmiṃ yeva āvibhavissati. Tasmā,

Here it may be asked: How then should it be understood that 'name-and-form is a condition for the six sense bases'? Because of the existence of the latter when the former exists. For when this or that name and form exist, this or that sense base comes to be, not otherwise. And its being conditioned by the existence of that will become evident in the exposition of the conditional method itself. Therefore:

Paṭisandhiyā pavatte vā, hoti yaṃ yassa paccayo;

Yathā ca paccayo hoti, tathā neyyaṃ vibhāvinā.

At rebirth-linking or during the course of life, whatever is a condition for whatever, and in what way it is a condition, so should it be understood by the discerning one.

Tatrāyamatthadīpanā –

Herein is the exposition of the meaning:

Nāmameva hi āruppe, paṭisandhipavattisu;

Paccayo sattadhā chadhā, hoti taṃ avakaṃsato.

In the formless realm, at rebirth-linking and during the course of life, nāma alone is a condition in seven or six ways, at a minimum.

Kathaṃ? Paṭisandhiyaṃ tāva avakaṃsato sahajātaaññamaññanissayasampayuttavipākaatthiavigatapaccayehi sattadhā nāmaṃ chaṭṭhāyatanassa paccayo hoti. Kiñci panettha hetupaccayena, kiñci āhārapaccayenāti evaṃ [M 2.0197] aññathāpi paccayo hoti, tassa vasena ukkaṃsāvakaṃso veditabbo.

How so? First, at rebirth-linking, at a minimum, nāma is a condition for the sixth sense base in seven ways: by way of conascence, mutuality, support, association, result, presence, and non-disappearance conditions. Herein, some part is a condition by way of root condition, some by way of nutriment condition; thus it is a condition in other ways as well. By means of that, the maximum and minimum range should be understood.

Pavattepi vipākaṃ vuttanayeneva paccayo hoti, itaraṃ pana avakaṃsato vuttappakāresu paccayesu vipākapaccayavajjehi chahi paccayehi paccayo hoti. Kiñci panettha hetupaccayena, kiñci āhārapaccayenāti evaṃ aññathāpi paccayo hoti, tassa vasena ukkaṃsāvakaṃso veditabbo.

During the course of life as well, resultant mentality is a condition in the very manner already stated. The other, non-resultant mentality, however, is, at a minimum, a condition by six conditions among those already described, excluding the resultant condition. Furthermore, herein some mentality is a condition by way of root condition, some by way of nutriment condition, and thus it is also a condition in other ways. By means of these conditions, the maximum and minimum applications should be understood.

Aññasmimpi [V 2.0195] bhave nāmaṃ, tatheva paṭisandhiyaṃ;

Chaṭṭhassa itaresaṃ taṃ, chahākārehi paccayo.

In another existence as well, at rebirth-linking, that mentality is a condition for the sixth base in that very same way. For the other bases, it is a condition in six ways.

Āruppato hi aññasmimpi pañcavokārabhave taṃ vipākanāmaṃ hadayavatthuno sahāyaṃ hutvā chaṭṭhassa manāyatanassa yathā āruppe vuttaṃ, tatheva avakaṃsato sattadhā paccayo hoti. Itaresaṃ pana taṃ pañcannaṃ cakkhāyatanādīnaṃ catumahābhūtasahāyaṃ hutvā sahajātanissayavipākavippayuttaatthiavigatavasena chahākārehi paccayo hoti. Kiñci panettha hetupaccayena, kiñci āhārapaccayenāti evaṃ aññathāpi paccayo hoti, tassa vasena ukkaṃsāvakaṃso veditabbo.

To elaborate, in another existence apart from the formless realm, that is, in the five-aggregate existence, that resultant mentality, having become a companion to the heart-base, is a condition for the sixth, the mind-base, just as was stated for the formless realm. Thus, at a minimum, it is a condition in seven ways. For the other five, the eye-base and so on, that resultant mentality, having become a companion to the four great elements, is a condition in six ways by means of co-nascence, dependence, resultance, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance. Furthermore, herein some mentality is a condition by way of root condition, some by way of nutriment condition, and thus it is also a condition in other ways. By means of these conditions, the maximum and minimum applications should be understood.

Pavattepi tathā hoti, pākaṃ pākassa paccayo;

Apākaṃ avipākassa, chadhā chaṭṭhassa paccayo.

During the course of life also, it is thus: resultant mentality is a condition for the resultant sixth base; non-resultant mentality is a condition for the non-resultant sixth base in six ways.

Pavattepi hi pañcavokārabhave yathā paṭisandhiyaṃ, tatheva vipākanāmaṃ vipākassa chaṭṭhāyatanassa avakaṃsato sattadhā paccayo hoti. Avipākaṃ pana avipākassa chaṭṭhassa avakaṃsatova tato vipākapaccayaṃ apanetvā chadhā paccayo hoti. Vuttanayeneva panettha ukkaṃsāvakaṃso veditabbo.

To elaborate, during the course of life in the five-aggregate existence, just as at rebirth-linking, so too resultant mentality is a condition for the resultant sixth sense-base, at a minimum, in seven ways. Non-resultant mentality, however, is a condition for the non-resultant sixth base, at a minimum, in six ways, by removing the resultant condition from those. Herein, the maximum and minimum applications should be understood in the very manner already stated.

Tattheva sesapañcannaṃ, vipākaṃ paccayo bhave;

Catudhā avipākampi, evameva pakāsitaṃ.

Right there, for the remaining five bases, resultant mentality would be a condition in four ways. Non-resultant mentality is also explained in this very same way.

Tattheva hi pavatte sesānaṃ cakkhāyatanādīnaṃ pañcannaṃ cakkhupasādādivatthukaṃ itarampi vipākanāmaṃ pacchājātavippayuttaatthiavigatapaccayehi catudhā paccayo hoti. Yathā ca vipākaṃ, avipākampi evameva pakāsitaṃ. Tasmā kusalādibhedampi tesaṃ catudhā paccayo hotīti veditabbaṃ. Evaṃ [M 2.0198] tāva nāmameva paṭisandhiyaṃ pavatte vā yassa yassa āyatanassa paccayo hoti, yathā ca paccayo hoti, tathā veditabbaṃ.

To elaborate, right there during the course of life, for the remaining five bases, the eye-base and so on, resultant mentality—both that which is based on eye-sensitivity, etc., and the other—is a condition in four ways by means of post-nascence, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance conditions. And just as the resultant is explained, so too is the non-resultant explained in the very same way. Therefore, it should be understood that mentality distinguished as wholesome, etc., is also a condition for them in four ways. Thus, it should first be understood for which particular sense-base mentality alone is a condition, whether at rebirth-linking or during the course of life, and in what manner it is a condition.

Rūpaṃ panettha āruppe, bhave bhavati paccayo;

Na ekāyatanassāpi, pañcakkhandhabhave pana.

Herein, in the formless existence, form is not a condition even for a single base; but in the five-aggregate existence, it is.

Rūpato [V 2.0196] sandhiyaṃ vatthu, chadhā chaṭṭhassa paccayo;

Bhūtāni catudhā honti, pañcannaṃ avisesato.

Among forms, at rebirth-linking, the physical base is a condition for the sixth base in six ways. The primary elements are conditions for the five bases in four ways, without distinction.

Rūpato hi paṭisandhiyaṃ vatthurūpaṃ chaṭṭhassa manāyatanassa sahajātaaññamaññanissayavippayuttaatthiavigatapaccayehi chadhā paccayo hoti. Cattāri pana bhūtāni avisesato paṭisandhiyaṃ pavatte ca yaṃ yaṃ āyatanaṃ uppajjati, tassa tassa vasena pañcannampi cakkhāyatanādīnaṃ sahajātanissayaatthiavigatapaccayehi catudhā paccayā honti.

To elaborate, among forms, at rebirth-linking, the physical base is a condition for the sixth, the mind-base, in six ways by means of co-nascence, mutuality, dependence, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance conditions. The four primary elements, however, without distinction—both at rebirth-linking and during the course of life—are conditions in four ways for all five bases, the eye-base and so on, according to whichever sense-base arises, by means of co-nascence, dependence, presence, and non-disappearance conditions.

Tidhā jīvitametesaṃ, āhāro ca pavattiyaṃ;

Tāneva chadhā chaṭṭhassa, vatthu tasseva pañcadhā.

The life faculty is a condition for these in three ways, and so is nutriment during the course of life. Those very five bases are conditions for the sixth base in six ways; the physical base is a condition for that same sixth base in five ways.

Etesaṃ pana cakkhādīnaṃ pañcannaṃ paṭisandhiyaṃ pavatte ca atthi avigataindriyavasena rūpajīvitaṃ tidhā paccayo hoti. Āhāro ca atthiavigatāhāravasena tividhā paccayo hoti, so ca kho ye sattā āhārūpajīvino, tesaṃ āhārānugate kāye pavattiyaṃyeva, no paṭisandhiyaṃ. Tāni pana pañca cakkhāyatanādīni chaṭṭhassa cakkhu sotaghānajivhākāyaviññāṇasaṅkhātassa manāyatanassa nissayapurejātaindriyavippayuttaatthiavigatavasena chahākārehi paccayā honti pavatte, no paṭisandhiyaṃ. Ṭhapetvā pana pañcaviññāṇāni tasseva avasesamanāyatanassa vatthurūpaṃ nissayapurejātavippayuttaatthiavigatavasena pañcadhā paccayo hoti pavatteyeva, no paṭisandhiyaṃ. Evaṃ rūpameva paṭisandhiyaṃ pavatte vā yassa yassa āyatanassa paccayo hoti, yathā ca paccayo hoti, tathā veditabbaṃ.

To elaborate, for these five bases, the eye-base and so on, both at rebirth-linking and during the course of life, the material life faculty is a condition in three ways by means of presence, non-disappearance, and faculty conditions. Nutriment is also a condition in three ways by means of presence, non-disappearance, and nutriment conditions; this, however, applies only during the course of life in a body sustained by nutriment for those beings who subsist on it, not at rebirth-linking. Furthermore, those five bases—the eye-base and so on—are conditions for the sixth, the mind-base (designated as eye-, ear-, nose-, tongue-, and body-consciousness), in six ways by means of dependence, pre-nascence, faculty, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance conditions; this applies during the course of life, not at rebirth-linking. Excluding the five consciousnesses, the physical base is a condition for that remaining mind-base in five ways by means of dependence, pre-nascence, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance conditions; this applies only during the course of life, not at rebirth-linking. Thus, it should be understood for which particular sense-base materiality alone is a condition, whether at rebirth-linking or during the course of life, and in what manner it is a condition.

Nāmarūpaṃ panubhayaṃ, hoti yaṃ yassa paccayo;

Yathā ca tampi sabbattha, viññātabbaṃ vibhāvinā.

Now, as for both name-and-form, for whichever base it is a condition, and in what manner it is a condition—that too should be understood in all instances by one who is discerning.

Seyyathidaṃ[M 2.0199]. Paṭisandhiyaṃ tāva pañcavokārabhave khandhattayavatthurūpasaṅkhātaṃ nāmarūpaṃ chaṭṭhāyatanassa sahajātaaññamaññanissayavipākasampayuttavippayuttaatthiavigatapaccayādīhi paccayo hotīti. Idamettha mukhamattaṃ. Vuttanayānusārena pana sakkā sabbaṃ yojetunti na ettha vitthāro dassitoti.

As follows: Firstly, at rebirth-linking in the five-aggregate existence, name-and-form—designated as the three aggregates and the physical base—is a condition for the sixth sense-base by means of co-nascence, mutuality, dependence, resultance, association, dissociation, presence, non-disappearance conditions, and so on. This here is merely an introduction. However, by following the method already stated, it is possible to apply it to everything; therefore, a detailed explanation is not given here.

Ayaṃ “nāmarūpapaccayā saḷāyatana”nti padasmiṃ vitthārakathā.

This is the detailed explanation on the phrase 'nāmarūpapaccayā saḷāyatanaṃ' (the six sense-bases as conditioned by name-and-form).

Saḷāyatanapaccayāphassapadavitthārakathā

The Detailed Explanation of the Phrase 'Saḷāyatanapaccayā Phasso' (Contact as Conditioned by the Six Sense-Bases).

642. Saḷāyatanapaccayā [V 2.0197] phassapade –

642. In the phrase 'saḷāyatanapaccayā phasso' (contact as conditioned by the six sense-bases):

Saḷeva phassā saṅkhepā, cakkhusamphassaādayo;

Viññāṇamiva bāttiṃsa, vitthārena bhavanti te.

In brief, there are just six contacts, beginning with eye-contact. In detail, like consciousness, they become thirty-two.

Saṅkhepena hi saḷāyatanapaccayā phassoti cakkhusamphasso, sotasamphasso, ghānasamphasso, jivhāsamphasso, kāyasamphasso, manosamphassoti ime cakkhusamphassādayo cha eva phassā bhavanti. Vitthārena pana cakkhusamphassādayo pañca kusalavipākā, pañca akusalavipākāti dasa, sesā bāvīsati-lokiyavipākaviññāṇasampayuttā ca bāvīsatīti evaṃ sabbepi saṅkhārapaccayā vuttaviññāṇamiva bāttiṃsa honti.

In brief, 'contact conditioned by the six sense-bases' refers to eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact. These are the only six contacts, beginning with eye-contact. In detail, however, the five beginning with eye-contact are five wholesome-resultants and five unwholesome-resultants, thus making ten. The remaining twenty-two, being associated with the twenty-two mundane resultant consciousnesses, also amount to twenty-two. Thus, all of them, like the consciousness spoken of as conditioned by formations, become thirty-two.

Yaṃ panetassa bāttiṃsavidhassāpi phassassa paccayo saḷāyatanaṃ, tattha,

Now, with regard to the six sense-bases which are the condition for this thirty-twofold contact, therein,

Chaṭṭhena saha ajjhattaṃ, cakkhādiṃ bāhirehipi;

Saḷāyatanamicchanti, chahi saddhiṃ vicakkhaṇā.

The wise hold the six sense-bases to be the internal eye-base, etc., with the sixth, and also together with the six external bases.

Tattha ye tāva “upādiṇṇakapavattikathā aya”nti sakasantatipariyāpannameva paccayaṃ paccayuppannañca dīpenti, te “chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso”ti (vibha. 322) pāḷianusārato āruppe chaṭṭhāyatanañca, aññattha sabbasaṅgahato saḷāyatanañca phassassa paccayoti ekadesasarūpekasesaṃ katvā chaṭṭhena saha ajjhattaṃ cakkhādiṃ saḷāyatananti icchanti. Tañhi chaṭṭhāyatanañca saḷāyatanañca saḷāyatanantveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati.

Therein, firstly, those who explain the condition and the conditioned as being included only within one’s own continuity, thinking, 'This is a discourse on the process of what is appropriated by kamma,' follow the Pāli text, 'Conditioned by the sixth sense-base is contact' (Vibh. 322). They hold that in the formless realm the sixth sense-base, and elsewhere the six sense-bases by way of complete inclusion, are the condition for contact. Thus, by making a compound where one part of similar form remains, they hold that the six sense-bases are the internal eye-base and so on, together with the sixth. For indeed, 'the sixth sense-base' and 'the six sense-bases' are reckoned simply as 'the six sense-bases'.

Ye pana paccayuppannameva ekasantatipariyāpannaṃ dīpenti, paccayaṃ pana bhinnasantānampi, te yaṃ yaṃ āyatanaṃ phassassa paccayo hoti, taṃ sabbampi [M 2.0200] dīpentā bāhirampi pariggahetvā tadeva chaṭṭhena saha ajjhattaṃ bāhirehipi rūpāyatanādīhi saddhiṃ saḷāyatananti icchanti. Tampi hi chaṭṭhāyatanañca saḷāyatanañca saḷāyatananti etesaṃ ekasese kate saḷāyatanantveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati.

But those who explain only the conditioned effect as included within one continuity, while the condition may belong to a different continuity—they, in explaining every sense-base that is a condition for contact, also include the external. They hold that the six sense-bases are that very internal eye-base, etc., together with the sixth, and also together with the external form-base and so on. For that too—'the sixth sense-base,' 'the six [internal] sense-bases,' and 'the six [external] sense-bases'—when an ellipsis is made of these, is reckoned simply as 'the six sense-bases'.

Etthāha [V 2.0198] – na sabbāyatanehi eko phasso sambhoti, nāpi ekamhā āyatanā sabbe phassā, ayañca saḷāyatanapaccayā phassoti ekova vutto, so kasmāti. Tatridaṃ vissajjanaṃ – saccametaṃ, sabbehi eko, ekamhā vā sabbe na sambhonti, sambhoti pana anekehi eko. Yathā cakkhusamphasso cakkhāyatanā rūpāyatanā cakkhuviññāṇasaṅkhātā manāyatanā avasesasampayuttadhammāyatanā cāti evaṃ sabbattha yathānurūpaṃ yojetabbaṃ. Tasmā eva hi,

Here one asks: 'A single contact does not arise from all sense-bases, nor do all contacts arise from a single sense-base. Yet this, 'contact conditioned by the six sense-bases,' is stated in the singular. Why is that?' Here is the answer: It is true that a single contact does not arise from all bases, nor do all contacts from a single base. However, a single contact does arise from many bases. For example, eye-contact arises from the eye-base, the form-base, the mind-base designated as eye-consciousness, and the dhamma-base of remaining associated states. In this way, it should be applied appropriately in all cases. Therefore, indeed,

Ekopanekāyatanappabhavo iti dīpito;

Phassoyaṃ ekavacananiddesenīdha tādinā.

This contact, though one, originates from many bases; thus it is shown here by the Such-like One with a singular expression.

Ekavacananiddesenāti saḷāyatanapaccayā phassoti iminā ekavacananiddesena anekehi āyatanehi eko phasso hotīti tādinā dīpitoti attho. Āyatanesu pana,

'By a singular expression' means: by this singular expression, 'contact conditioned by the six sense-bases,' it is shown by the Such-like One that one contact arises from many bases. This is the meaning. Now, regarding the sense-bases:

Chadhā pañca tato ekaṃ, navadhā bāhirāni cha;

Yathāsambhavametassa, paccayatte vibhāvaye.

One should analyze the conditionality for this contact: the five in six ways, then the one in nine ways, and the six external bases according to what is possible.

Tatrāyaṃ vibhāvanā – cakkhāyatanādīni tāva pañca cakkhusamphassādibhedato pañcavidhassa phassassa nissayapurejātindriyavippayuttaatthiavigatavasena chadhā paccayā honti. Tato paraṃ ekaṃ vipākamanāyatanaṃ anekabhedassa vipākamanosamphassassa sahajātaaññamaññanissayavipākāhāraindriyasampayuttaatthiavigatavasena navadhā paccayo hoti. Bāhiresu pana rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhusamphassassa ārammaṇapurejātaatthiavigatavasena catudhā paccayo hoti. Tathā saddāyatanādīni sotasamphassādīnaṃ. Manosamphassassa pana tāni ca dhammāyatanañca tathā ca [M 2.0201] ārammaṇapaccayamatteneva cāti evaṃ bāhirāni cha yathāsambhavametassa paccayatte vibhāvayeti.

Herein, this is the analysis: Firstly, the five sense-bases beginning with the eye-base are conditions in six ways for the five kinds of contact, which begin with eye-contact, by way of dependence, pre-nascence, faculty, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance. Then, the one resultant mind-base is a condition in nine ways for the manifold resultant mind-contact by way of conascence, mutuality, dependence, result, nutriment, faculty, association, presence, and non-disappearance. Among the external bases, the form-base is a condition in four ways for eye-contact by way of object, pre-nascence, presence, and non-disappearance. Likewise for the sound-base, etc., with regard to ear-contact, etc. For mind-contact, however, those bases and the dhamma-base are conditions both in that same fourfold way and also merely by way of the object condition. Thus, one should analyze the conditionality of the six external bases for this contact according to what is possible.

Ayaṃ “saḷāyatanapaccayā phasso”ti padasmiṃ vitthārakathā.

This is the detailed discourse on the phrase, 'Conditioned by the six sense-bases is contact.'

Phassapaccayāvedanāpadavitthārakathā

The Detailed Discourse on the Phrase 'Conditioned by Contact is Feeling'

643. Phassapaccayā vedanāpade –

643. In the phrase 'Conditioned by contact is feeling':

Dvārato [V 2.0199] vedanā vuttā, cakkhusamphassajādikā;

Saḷeva tā pabhedena, ekūnanavutī matā.

Feelings are spoken of by way of the doors, beginning with that born of eye-contact; they are just six. But by way of detailed division, they are considered to be eighty-nine.

Etassapi padassa vibhaṅge “cakkhusamphassajā vedanā. Sota… ghāna… jivhā… kāya… manosamphassajā vedanā”ti (vibha. 231) evaṃ dvārato saḷeva vedanā vuttā, tā pana pabhedena ekūnanavutiyā cittehi sampayuttattā ekūnanavuti matā.

In the Vibhaṅga's analysis of this phrase, 'feeling born of eye-contact... feeling born of mind-contact' (Vibh. 231), just six feelings are spoken of by way of the doors. However, by way of detailed division, they are considered to be eighty-nine because of their association with eighty-nine consciousnesses.

Vedanāsu panetāsu, idha bāttiṃsa vedanā;

Vipākacittayuttāva, adhippetāti bhāsitā.

But among these feelings, it is said that here thirty-two feelings are intended, namely only those associated with resultant consciousness.

Aṭṭhadhā tattha pañcannaṃ, pañcadvāramhi paccayo;

Sesānaṃ ekadhā phasso, manodvārepi so tathā.

Therein, for the five in the five-door process, contact is a condition in eight ways; for the remainder, in one way. In the mind-door process, it is likewise.

Tattha hi pañcadvāre cakkhupasādādivatthukānaṃ pañcannaṃ vedanānaṃ cakkhusamphassādiko phasso sahajātaaññamaññanissayavipākaāhārasampayuttaatthiavigatavasena aṭṭhadhā paccayo hoti. Sesānaṃ pana ekekasmiṃ dvāre sampaṭicchanasantīraṇatadārammaṇavasena pavattānaṃ kāmāvacaravipākavedanānaṃ so cakkhusamphassādiko phasso upanissayavasena ekadhāva paccayo hoti.

For therein, in the five-door process, for the five feelings that have the eye-sensitivity, etc., as their physical basis, the contact beginning with eye-contact is a condition in eight ways: by way of conascence, mutuality, dependence, result, nutriment, association, presence, and non-disappearance. For the remaining sense-sphere resultant feelings, however, which proceed in each door by way of receiving, investigating, and registering, that contact beginning with eye-contact is a condition in one way only: by way of decisive support.
